# `swarm` — session mode and task waves (OMP, Devin)

Two entry points, one file. Standalone: `/swarm on|off|<task>` (OMP
`/skill:swarm`, Devin `/swarm`) through the `~/.agents/skills/swarm` link.
From the `tower` bundle: Kimi CLI loads it as `/tower.swarm on|off|<task>`;
OMP invokes `/tower swarm on|off|<task>`, and the tower parent reads this file
because neither OMP nor Devin recursively discovers skills. Every
`/tower swarm X` below is equally `/swarm X`. The validator lives in the
UFO-FSD checkout: run it from `$UFO_ROOT`, else `~/Projects/ufo-fsd-alpha`;
without that checkout there is no validator, so execute directly or plan only,
and say which.

## Session toggle

- `/tower swarm on` (Kimi CLI: `/tower.swarm on`) enables swarm-wave behavior
  for this conversation only; confirm the session state. `/tower swarm off`
  (`/tower.swarm off`) disables it and confirm. This is conversational state
  only: do not write OMP configuration or claim a
  persistent toggle API. The toggle never makes a wave the orchestrator — a
  wave stays a dispatch shape for independent, unjudged work, not a session
  mode with authority over the parent.
- When enabled, consider a validated wave for a large set of independent,
  similarly shaped, unjudged tasks with disjoint ownership. It is not a general
  replacement for ordinary `task` delegation. Use normal delegation for a small
  set, one-off task, overlapping edits, work requiring one shared writer, or any
  request that cannot meet the wave validator's shape and bounds. Never split a
  wave into several `task` calls to evade a refusal.
- `/tower swarm <task>` (Kimi CLI: `/tower.swarm <task>`) requests one wave
  attempt; loading this skill without a task explains the toggle and asks for
  an actionable task specification. Never
  manufacture work or split one user's task into artificial lanes merely to hit
  the minimum. Size to the work inside the band: N same-shape items are one wave
  of N when the band admits N, sequential waves of at most the ceiling when N
  exceeds it (fold a short tail into the previous wave), and direct execution
  when N falls under the floor — padding to the floor is forbidden.

## Validate, then dispatch exactly once

1. Declare a spec with distinct per-item prompts or a template containing
   `{{item}}`; use a saved spec, stdin, or inline JSON. Validate it with
   `node scripts/ufo-swarm-wave.mjs plan --spec-json '<JSON>'` (or `--spec PATH`
   / `--spec -` for a file/stdin), which emits the plan without dispatching, and
   render the dispatch payload with `run` on the same spec arguments.
   `record --registry <path> --assignments <json>` fills in agent ids once the
   task call returns them. Do not dispatch if validation refuses the spec.
2. Read the `ufo-swarm-wave-dispatch-v1` result. Make **one** OMP `task` tool
   call using its `taskCall.context` and complete `taskCall.tasks` array as-is.
   If `taskCall` is `null`, there are no new spawn tasks: send each
   `resumeSends` entry to its recorded parked agent as
   `hub send --to <entry.resume> --message <entry.message>` — `entry.name` is
   bookkeeping, not a hub field. Resume is continuity to an existing agent, not
   a fresh spawn or a second wave. Each `taskCall.tasks` entry is exactly
   `{name, agent, task}` — `agent` is the lane's taxonomy role, `task` its
   composed text, and there is no per-lane model key. Do not invent, omit, or
   rewrite lanes, roles, bindings, or resumes after validation.

   **On Devin** the validated payload is the same; only the plumbing maps.
   Issue every spawn lane as its own `run_subagent` call, all in **one**
   response (that response is the wave), each with `is_background: true`,
   `title` = the lane's `name`, `task` = `taskCall.context`, a blank line,
   then the lane's `task`, and `profile` = `ufo-<agent>`. If that profile is
   not installed, use `subagent_explore` for `scout`, `reviewer`, `critic`,
   `sentinel`, `connector`, and `revenger`, and `subagent_general` for
   `executor`, `simplifier`, `scribe`, and `mutation-tester`, and say so in
   the report. The one permitted edit to rendered text: insert the bytes of
   `~/.agents/skills/godspeed/directive.md` directly after each task's
   leading `/skill:godspeed` line, because Devin injects nothing. A
   `resumeSends` entry becomes `run_subagent` with `resume: <entry.resume>`
   and `task: <entry.message>`, unprefixed. Feed the returned agent ids to
   `record --assignments`. Never pass a model.
3. Integrate and report only observed results. Workers advise the parent; keep
   one L1, no second judge, honest evidence, and no concurrent overlapping-file
   assignments. Wave output is advisory: no lane becomes a judge verdict.

The validator is normative. The configured wave band is **16–32 total members**
(spawn lanes plus resumes counted together) **per wave**, from
`sighting.dispatch.swarm.waveMinLanes`/`waveMaxLanes`; the per-L1 member
ceiling `swarm.maxLanes` is **100** — the round budget that sequential waves of
one round share, and the cap the validator enforces on any single wave — and a
per-spec `maxLanes` may only tighten it, never widen it. `swarm.minLanes` **16**
is the declared swarm-round floor — policy, not a planner gate; what the
planner gates is the wave band, and in a band-less policy the built-in minimum
is **2**. Both wave-band gates fire only on spawn-bearing waves, so a
resume-only wave is exempt from the wave floor *and* the wave ceiling and is
bounded only by the member cap; a spec cap below the floor makes a spawn wave
unreachable and fails before any lane spawns. Items must expand to
pairwise-distinct prompts; a duplicate expansion is a refusal, never a silent
dedupe. Refusals are typed, and this list is not their full set:
wave/band `empty_wave`, `too_few_lanes`, `wave_too_wide`, `too_many_lanes`,
`impossible_band`; lane/spec shape `duplicate_expansion`, `duplicate_name`,
`role_required`, `unknown_role`, `invalid_spec`, `invalid_policy`,
`invalid_registry`; resume `resume_unknown_member`, `duplicate_resume_id`,
`resume_role_forbidden`, `resume_item_forbidden`, `resume_meta_forbidden`,
`message_with_prompt`; and (with route preflight enabled)
`route_unreachable` — all raised by `plan`/`run` before a lane spawns; after
the task call returns ids, `record` adds `conflicting_assignment`,
`unknown_member` and `invalid_agent_id` plus the registry/assignment-shape
refusals (`invalid_registry`, `invalid_registry_path`, `invalid_assignments`).
A refusal is a reason to fix the spec or execute the work directly, never a
reason to bypass validation.

Devin uses the same live band unchanged (operator choice). Its
`nativeProfiles.devin-native-v1.concurrencyCeiling` in `config/ufo.json` is
how many lanes run at once, not a wave gate: never re-split a validated wave
to fit it. A lane Devin fails to start or that dies is a dead lane — reported
as such (I3) — not a reason to respawn it under a new identity.

Each new spawn carries one explicit taxonomy role: `scout`, `reviewer`,
`critic`, `connector`, `sentinel`, `executor`, `mutation-tester`, `revenger`,
`simplifier`, or `scribe`. Do not include frozen-topology seats (planner,
distiller, labrat, Main) as swarm roles. A spawn item may declare `axes` (1–8
distinct nonempty names, ≤256 bytes each) and a short `milestone`; spec-level
values are defaults, item-level wins, and a resume lane inherits the spawn
binding rather than supplying its own.

Resume assignments must name an owned member from the wave registry or the
spec's declared `priorRegistry`; unknown ids fail closed as
`resume_unknown_member` before any lane spawns, while conflicting handles fail
closed at `record`, after the task call returns ids. Keep and use the
validator's registry and dispatch output for continuity — the registry records
each spawn member's name, agent id, item and role; a resume row names its owner
and inherits that binding, with its own `agentId` deliberately null so the
original spawn row stays the handle's sole owner. That is what lets a later wave
resume a member by its recorded agent id across turns. A resumed agent retains
its existing identity and role; do not assign it a new role or a replacement
agent. OMP's one `task` call is the wave, so kimi's 5-per-700ms launch ramp
needs no porting: the harness queues lanes beyond its own concurrency window,
and the ramp constants are recorded in the plan as declared pacing policy
only.

## Lane shape: leaf by default

A swarm member is a leaf — no delegation and no background jobs. Omit the
`spawns:` key entirely for a leaf; `spawns: []` is a footgun, not the leaf
spelling, because an empty list collapses to undefined and yields a wildcard
when `task` is in the lane's tools. `agents/executor.md` is the one card that
permits a spawn (`labrat`), and the host's `task.maxRecursionDepth` (**2**) is
what bounds that chain. The host's `task.maxConcurrency` (**32**) is a separate
cap on lanes running at once; it is not the wave band and not the member
ceiling — the host cap bounds how many lanes run at once, never how wide one
wave may be; the later waves of a full round are dispatched after the earlier
waves, and a wave never relies on the harness concurrency queue to hold its
lanes.

## Godspeed posture

Every fresh spawn lane carries `/skill:godspeed` as its leading line: the wave
renderer injects it, and — in any session rooted where the hook is installed —
the OMP `task` hook (`.omp/hooks/pre/ufo-godspeed-inject.js`) enforces it for
every `task` dispatch, batched or flat, idempotently. The hook is
project-scoped (`<cwd>/.omp/hooks/pre/`), so dispatching from a repo without it
leaves the renderer as the only guarantee, and eval-kernel `agent()`/
`workpool()` spawns bypass the `task` tool entirely and must prepend the
invocation themselves. Resume `hub send` entries never carry
it — a resume continues an existing session, and a stacked invocation would
reach a lane twice. The posture in one line: **name the axes, iterate cheap and
in parallel, keep moves that improve any axis and harm none, and never stall in
clarifying-question loops.** It governs how a lane works inside its own item; it
does not widen the lane's scope, let it judge, or let it spawn.

## Routing and observation

- The taxonomy role selects its `@m_*`/role alias bucket through the operator's
  bound global OMP `~/.omp/agent/config.yml` (`task.agentModelOverrides`,
  `modelRoles`, and `retry.fallbackChains`); it binds each seat to a bucket
  alias — the approved table is three (`m_strong`, `m_mid`, `m_fast`), with
  other `m_*` aliases declared as named lanes, and the live table rather than
  this file decides the binding. Any alias and ordered fallback chain may be
  used **only through OMP routing and authentication already configured by the
  operator**. The global config is the sole routing/auth authority. Never
  hardcode a provider/model, credentials, or a per-lane model param — there is
  no per-lane model knob. Opt-in route preflight (`--route-families`, on `plan`
  and `run`) flags a wave whose pinned lanes resolve into one route family
  carrying more than one lane as `singleFamily` (roles with no seat override
  are reported unpinned and never attributed), so you can split it or record the
  accepted risk; never edit or override global routing from this skill.
- On Devin there is no alias table: the lane's `ufo-<role>` profile carries
  no `model:` and runs on Devin's default subagent model, while the
  `subagent_general` fallback runs on the parent's model (a full wave of it
  multiplies premium spend — say so before dispatch). `--route-families`
  resolves OMP routes only and says nothing about Devin lanes; do not cite it
  as Devin route evidence.
- Use `scripts/ufo-sighting open` to open the operator wall (tmux session
  `ufo_sighting`, window 1); `status [--lite]` and `overview [--watch]` to
  inspect it; `peek --mission <id> [--lines N]` to read a pane back;
  `steer --mission <id> --text "<one line>"` to send operator input; and
  `complete --mission <id> [--note <text>]` to retire a registered mission.
  These are UFO Sighting display and interaction controls for registered
  missions, not swarm orchestration: the wall itself never dispatches, judges,
  or owns a wave. A `task` worker, Devin subagent, or swarm lane is **not** automatically a wall
  mission or titled pane.
- `launch … --fleet NAME ... -- <command>` opens a separate tmux window named
  after that fleet inside the session, one pane per registered mission — use
  `--fleet` for the registered fleet missions a launcher actually starts, and
  do not claim it exposes task workers.
- A registered fleet mission is the one wall mission that does dispatch and
  judge: `sighting/tower-fleet.mjs <verb> --spec <fleet.json>` renders
  `sighting/l1-prompt.md` into a fleet L1 pane that runs its own swarm waves.
  The verb is positional and comes first — omitting it selects `plan` (which
  writes nothing) — and the others are `launch --apply`, `status`, and `close
  --apply [--mission <id>]`. A mutation verb without `--apply` refuses with
  typed `MUTATION_REQUIRES_APPLY` before touching the wall or the filesystem,
  and every refusal is a typed `{ok:false, code, message}` envelope (exit 2;
  usage exit 64). Most of them — `INVALID_SPEC`, `L1_CEILING_EXCEEDED`,
  `PANE_CEILING_EXCEEDED`, `SCOPE_OVERLAP`, `UNKNOWN_MISSION` and the rest —
  are raised before any mutation; the exception is `LAUNCH_PARTIAL`, which
  exits 2 after panes and state were already written. Each mission gets its own
  worktree at `<repo>/.tower/worktrees/<fleet>/<id>` on branch
  `tower/<fleet>/<id>`, reused rather than clobbered, and comes up as one
  interactive omp pane — `-p`/`--print`/`--mode` are refused by
  `INTERACTIVE_GUARD`, and the pane's argv keeps `--cwd` equal to its own
  worktree. The launcher reads its authority once per invocation from
  `<ufoRoot>/config/ufo.json` — `dispatch.swarm.waveMinLanes`/`waveMaxLanes`/
  `maxLanes`, `dispatch.maxConcurrentL1`, `sighting.windowPaneCeiling` and
  `dispatch.missionFormat.l1Alias`, never `dispatch.globalRunnerCeiling` or
  `swarm.minLanes` — and refuses `CONFIG_UNREADABLE` before any mutation.
- The fleet pane carries a per-pane alias binding: the launcher passes
  `--model @<sighting.dispatch.missionFormat.l1Alias>` and
  `--config <ufoRoot>/config/mission-nightcall.yml`. That alias names a bucket
  in the operator's global routing table, not a provider/model, so the
  no-per-lane-knob rule above still holds for every lane.
- Three separate limits, none interchangeable: `sighting.windowPaneCeiling` is
  the enforced mission capacity of a fleet window (the default wall never reads
  it — its own capacity is display geometry, `layouts` rows × columns),
  `sighting.dispatch.maxConcurrentL1` is the live L1 mission ceiling, and
  `sighting.dispatch.globalRunnerCeiling` is the global runner ceiling.
  `close --apply` retires wall missions only; it never removes a worktree, and
  its human-readable output prints the exact
  `git -C <repo> worktree remove <path>` per mission.

The planner, taxonomy, registry, route authority, and Sighting behavior above
follow the project UFO skill, `scripts/ufo-swarm-wave.mjs`,
`sighting/tower-fleet.mjs`, `config/ufo.json`, and the repository routing
authority; defer to their current validator, config values, and operator-bound
global configuration rather than to any number or verb restated here.

- The taxonomy role selects its `@m_*`/role alias bucket through the operator's
  bound global OMP `~/.omp/agent/config.yml` (`task.agentModelOverrides`,
  `modelRoles`, and `retry.fallbackChains`); it binds each seat to a bucket
  alias — the approved table is three (`m_strong`, `m_mid`, `m_fast`), with
  other `m_*` aliases declared as named lanes, and the live table rather than
  this file decides the binding. Any alias and ordered fallback chain may be
  used **only through OMP routing and authentication already configured by the
  operator**. The global config is the sole routing/auth authority. Never
  hardcode a provider/model, credentials, or a per-lane model param — there is
  no per-lane model knob. Opt-in route preflight (`--route-families`, on `plan`
  and `run`) flags a wave whose pinned lanes resolve into one route family
  carrying more than one lane as `singleFamily` (roles with no seat override
  are reported unpinned and never attributed), so you can split it or record the
  accepted risk; never edit or override global routing from this skill.
- On Devin there is no alias table: the lane's `ufo-<role>` profile carries
  no `model:` and runs on Devin's default subagent model, while the
  `subagent_general` fallback runs on the parent's model (a full wave of it
  multiplies premium spend — say so before dispatch). `--route-families`
  resolves OMP routes only and says nothing about Devin lanes; do not cite it
  as Devin route evidence.
- Use `scripts/ufo-sighting open` to open the operator wall (tmux session
  `ufo_sighting`, window 1); `status [--lite]` and `overview [--watch]` to
  inspect it; `peek --mission <id> [--lines N]` to read a pane back;
  `steer --mission <id> --text "<one line>"` to send operator input; and
  `complete --mission <id> [--note <text>]` to retire a registered mission.
  These are UFO Sighting display and interaction controls for registered
  missions, not swarm orchestration: the wall itself never dispatches, judges,
  or owns a wave. A `task` worker, Devin subagent, or swarm lane is **not** automatically a wall
  mission or titled pane.
- `launch … --fleet NAME ... -- <command>` opens a separate tmux window named
  after that fleet inside the session, one pane per registered mission — use
  `--fleet` for the registered fleet missions a launcher actually starts, and
  do not claim it exposes task workers.
- A registered fleet mission is the one wall mission that does dispatch and
  judge: `sighting/tower-fleet.mjs <verb> --spec <fleet.json>` renders
  `sighting/l1-prompt.md` into a fleet L1 pane that runs its own swarm waves.
  The verb is positional and comes first — omitting it selects `plan` (which
  writes nothing) — and the others are `launch --apply`, `status`, and `close
  --apply [--mission <id>]`. A mutation verb without `--apply` refuses with
  typed `MUTATION_REQUIRES_APPLY` before touching the wall or the filesystem,
  and every refusal is a typed `{ok:false, code, message}` envelope (exit 2;
  usage exit 64). Most of them — `INVALID_SPEC`, `L1_CEILING_EXCEEDED`,
  `PANE_CEILING_EXCEEDED`, `SCOPE_OVERLAP`, `UNKNOWN_MISSION` and the rest —
  are raised before any mutation; the exception is `LAUNCH_PARTIAL`, which
  exits 2 after panes and state were already written. Each mission gets its own
  worktree at `<repo>/.tower/worktrees/<fleet>/<id>` on branch
  `tower/<fleet>/<id>`, reused rather than clobbered, and comes up as one
  interactive omp pane — `-p`/`--print`/`--mode` are refused by
  `INTERACTIVE_GUARD`, and the pane's argv keeps `--cwd` equal to its own
  worktree. The launcher reads its authority once per invocation from
  `<ufoRoot>/config/ufo.json` — `dispatch.swarm.waveMinLanes`/`waveMaxLanes`/
  `maxLanes`, `dispatch.maxConcurrentL1`, `sighting.windowPaneCeiling` and
  `dispatch.missionFormat.l1Alias`, never `dispatch.globalRunnerCeiling` or
  `swarm.minLanes` — and refuses `CONFIG_UNREADABLE` before any mutation.
- The fleet pane carries a per-pane alias binding: the launcher passes
  `--model @<sighting.dispatch.missionFormat.l1Alias>` and
  `--config <ufoRoot>/config/mission-nightcall.yml`. That alias names a bucket
  in the operator's global routing table, not a provider/model, so the
  no-per-lane-knob rule above still holds for every lane.
- Three separate limits, none interchangeable: `sighting.windowPaneCeiling` is
  the enforced mission capacity of a fleet window (the default wall never reads
  it — its own capacity is display geometry, `layouts` rows × columns),
  `sighting.dispatch.maxConcurrentL1` is the live L1 mission ceiling, and
  `sighting.dispatch.globalRunnerCeiling` is the global runner ceiling.
  `close --apply` retires wall missions only; it never removes a worktree, and
  its human-readable output prints the exact
  `git -C <repo> worktree remove <path>` per mission.

The planner, taxonomy, registry, route authority, and Sighting behavior above
follow the project UFO skill, `scripts/ufo-swarm-wave.mjs`,
`sighting/tower-fleet.mjs`, `config/ufo.json`, and the repository routing
authority; defer to their current validator, config values, and operator-bound
global configuration rather than to any number or verb restated here.

…

…
252:   - **Dispatch evidence** is the `.ufo/watchdog.log` dispatch line — `launch <lane> round=N`
…
263:     `live` test can never fail while its daemon is up (§Appendix, "Liveness probes").
264:     `in-flight` is therefore decided from
265:     the absence of both a `complete <lane> round=N` line and a *landed* report — an
266:     uncommitted file at the report path does not end `in-flight`, however it fires the driver's
267:     existence signal (§Appendix, "Unlanded report") — and never from a status probe.
268:     `.ufo/watchdog.log` is mutable and the driver appends to it concurrently, so its line numbers
269:     drift: the round notes carry a committed digest (timestamp + text) of every dispatch/complete
270:     line a status rests on, and that digest — not the live log — is the pointer that resolves at
271:     closure.
272:   - **`in-flight` is debt, not a resting status.** Every `in-flight` row is answered by the next
273:     protocol round — resolved to a terminal status or re-confirmed with evidence — which appends
274:     `{"round": N, "type": "closure-correction", "closed_at": …, "lanes": {<id>: <status>}}` — never
275:     an in-place edit. A lane dispatched for its Nth round *after* round `N` closed rides the next
276:     closure-correction for `N` — never dropped, never folded into `N+1`; an `in-flight` row still
277:     live at the next pass is re-confirmed by a closure-correction carrying `in-flight` plus the
278:     launch pointer and stays debt until the mission terminates.
279:   - No lane may be recorded `not-dispatched` while dispatch evidence for that lane-round exists,
280:     and no lane may be recorded `in-flight` unless its mission was live at `closed_at`. A row
281:     contradicting evidence is a conformance defect of the entry (§Appendix, "Closure entries").
282:   - **A row names the lane-round it describes.** `lanes` values stay status strings; the optional
283:     `lane_rounds: {<id>: <n>}` map records a lane's own counter where it differs from the entry's
284:     `round` and is required on every `not-dispatched` row. The row describes lane-round `(<id>,
285:     round)`: `lane_rounds` annotates it and never re-keys it, so
286:     last-wins is computed over `(id, entry.round)`; reading the map as the key erases in-flight
287:     debt and manufactures rows out of the pre-fleet-2 fleet-keyed entries, which
288:     carry no `lane_rounds` and are `unadjudicable` as lane-rounds (§Appendix, "Row identity"). An
289:     `ok` row needs no pointer — `.ufo/reports/round-<n>/<id>.md` is derivable, and its absence
290:     falsifies the row. `failed`, `in-flight`, and `not-dispatched` rows carry their pointer in
291:     `notes`.
292:   - **Retroactive closure is typed, and is not a pass.** Entries for lane-rounds that terminated
293:     before the integrator role existed carry `type: "retroactive-closure"` and notes stating that
294:     the statuses are presence-of-evidence only, that step-1 verification (hash ancestry, `SHONEN`
295:     heading, prompt fidelity) did not run at the time, and — for rounds before fleet-2 (`609ecb6`)
296:     — that no axis-move duty existed. Promotion and axis reviews must never read a retroactive row
297:     as a contemporaneous pass.
298:   - **`rounds` is append-only after closure.** Corrections are appended entries carrying `type:
299:     "closure-correction"` and `supersedes: {round, type, date}` naming the row they replace — never
300:     in-place edits, never prepends, because index citations into the array must keep resolving.
301:     Where two corrections share round+type+date that triple names no unique row, so `supersedes`
302:     MAY also carry `entry` — the array index, stable precisely because the array is append-only —
303:     and a gate treats a correction that needs the disambiguator and omits it as ambiguous
304:     (§Appendix, "Append-only `rounds`"). Consumers read the array in order; `rounds[].round` is not
305:     unique and the last row for a lane wins.
306:   - **History is pinned.** `.ufo/history-pin.json` pins `sha256(rounds[0:k])` for the closed prefix
307:     plus the commit whose `MANIFEST.json` bytes hash to it; the closure gate reports
308:     `history_pin_mismatch` when closed history was edited in place and `history_pin_unanchored`
309:     when the pin was regenerated to bless an edit. Appends never invalidate it.
310:The **aggregator** lane is a main-repo lane that reviews every child repo's `corpus/` each round
311:(per `CORPUS.md`), files gaps as lessons inside the child repos, and files its own round report at
312:`.ufo/reports/round-<N>/aggregator.md`. Its report covers per-repo corpus verdicts and cross-lane
313:learnings. It is the sole exception to lane write-scope: it may create or repair `corpus/` inside any
314:child repo, and nothing else — no main-repo files outside its own report and ledger. Every file it
315:creates inside a child repo is **committed by the aggregator itself at creation time**, pathspec-limited
316:to its own files, under its own subject (`corpus: round-<N> aggregator …`) — never left uncommitted for
317:a lane's round commit to sweep, and a lane never commits an aggregator-owned file. Alongside the
318:per-round report it maintains one rolling audit ledger — canonically `.ufo/reports/AGGREGATE.md`,
319:and no third path counts; a superseded
320:snapshot elsewhere is relocated there by its next refresh and remains readable evidence, superseded
321:and not voided. While the canonical ledger is absent or unrefreshed, the integrator's round notes
322:are the queue of record (§Appendix, "Ledger"). The ledger is append-only in the same sense as
323:`LOG.md` — refresh sections supersede earlier rows explicitly rather than rewriting them. An
324:aggregator round report is incomplete unless the ledger was refreshed or the report names why no row
325:changed. A round filed without the ledger duty keeps the routed-defect queue empty by construction.
326:
327:## Evidence standard
328:
329:Everywhere the protocol says *evidence*, it means a resolvable pointer: a repo path, a command and
330:its output, a commit, or an external document — never a naked assertion. A `LOG.md` entry without a
331:pointer is not evidence; an unreachable claim in a lane report does not exist.
332:An **end-to-end domain task** is one real work item executed against the domain's actual surfaces,
333:logged as trigger → action → outcome → pointer. Where the domain's terminal action is operator-owned
334:(§Invariants, local-first), executed means *prepared + verified + handed off*: the handoff artifact
335:is the outcome pointer, and a documented negative result at that gate still counts.
336:A numeric claim carries its counting command, an absence claim its search sweep, and a quote its
337:location (frontmatter/body, file, line) — the `CORPUS.md` rules bind `LOG.md` entries and lane
338:reports too, not only `corpus/`. A status command printing configured values is not evidence of
339:capability: endpoint/ability claims need a probe against the real surface.
340:An evidence pointer must resolve at *closure* time, not only at write time: paths under `tmpfs`
341:(`/tmp`, `/dev/shm`), session-scoped `local://` artifacts, and any pointer a fresh session cannot
342:reach are not evidence — commit the artifact or cite a reproducible command. A timestamp on evidence
343:must be at or before the commit that ships it — future-dated evidence is a conformance defect
344:(§Appendix, "Evidence standard").
345:- **Claimed ≠ re-executed.** A command offered as evidence is a re-run performed at write time with
346:  its observed output — never an output quoted from memory or a prior session.
347:- **Corrections sweep every mention.** Before a round's commit, grep every file the lane touches
348:  (`corpus/README.md`, `SKILL.md`, `knowledge/`) for the superseded claim — a corrected fact left
349:  standing in a sibling file is still a defect.
350:- **A falsified claim in an append-only file gets a named correction entry in the lane's next
351:  round** — appended, never rewritten; it stays on the routed-defect queue until it lands.
352:- **Commits are cited by hash, never by subject or tag** — `git rev-parse round-4` fails wherever
353:  the tag doesn't exist.
354:- **Drift pins.** A pin counts only if its expected values are **persisted inside the repo** (a
355:  recorded sha/mode/lines baseline, or a committed expected-output file the script diffs against); a
356:  fingerprint *printer* with no stored baseline cannot detect drift; a pin is `RECOMMENDED` where the
357:  cited surface is outside the lane's control.
358:
359:## Gate standard
360:
361:A **gate** is a committed, re-runnable verdict script a lane owns: it reads surfaces, compares them
362:against expected values persisted in its own repo, and returns a verdict. A tool that cannot fail is
363:a **probe**, and is registered as one.
364:- **Verdict.** `0` = `clean` and `1` = `failed` fleet-wide; every other code a gate exits (`2`, `3`,
365:  `64`, …) is declared in its registry entry and mapped onto `clean | failed | could-not-evaluate`,
366:  and an undeclared nonzero code reads as `could-not-evaluate`. Nothing else is pinned: a gate's own
367:  vocabulary — WARN vs HIT, a missing baseline, finding kinds — stays lane-owned, and this section
368:  governs the outer interface only.
369:- **Self-test.** Every gate exposes a self-invocation mode over isolated fixtures (temp trees, no
370:  network, no live-tree write) asserting both the exit code and a stable expected finding-id, with
371:  the expected values committed in the owning repo and independent of the recomputation. The flag
372:  spelling is the lane's (`--selftest`, `--self-test`, `run_selftest()`)
373:  and the registry records it; a helper-only or model-only self-check does not satisfy this clause.
374:- **Two evidences.** Self-test green is capability, not a measurement (§Evidence standard). A gate
375:  whose verdict depends on a mutable fleet artifact also ships a run over a committed input snapshot
376:  with its committed expected verdict, so a later hand-edit of that artifact contradicts the frozen
377:  run. A verdict names the revision it was measured against: a gate grades the tree it runs on, so a
378:  run over a moving worktree is not comparable to one over the cited commit. A frozen baseline's
379:  `expected.json` MUST pin the digest of every snapshot input file, and the gate verifies those
380:  digests before comparing verdicts: an edited snapshot is `snapshot_tampered` (could-not-evaluate),
381:  not a compared verdict, and a baseline without digests is reported `unpinned (legacy)`.
382:- **Registry.** The schema is this section's; the rows live in each lane's `SKILL.md`: name,
383:  `gate|probe`, entry command, verdict map (code → class), self-test command and spelling,
384:  pinned-value path, write scope, owner. The aggregator ledger stays the routed-defect queue, not a
385:  second inventory; a fleet index is pointers to lane rows, never copied expected values. Frozen
386:  baseline names resolve under any `.ufo/waves/*/frozen` root; a bare name matching more than one
387:  root fails closed.
388:- **Scope.** Read-only over surfaces it does not own, and it never acts on an external surface —
389:  publishing, vault approval, claim submission and driver mutation stay operator-owned (§Invariants,
390:  local-first). A verdict is lane-local evidence: it
391:  never defines the host runtime's stop conditions (`loop_stop`/`mission_goal`) and
392:  never stands in for the native judge.
393:- **Closure consequence.** A red gate is a conformance defect recorded in the round notes and routed
394:  to its owner — status-neutral unless the round's rules already prescribe `failed`; gate redness is
395:  never the marker predicate, since step 1 grades marker-versus-real-report first and only a marker
396:  invokes `failed`. The integrator verifies a gate's *committed evidence* (self-test tally,
397:  frozen-run verdict, the revision measured); it does not execute a sibling's gate, whose
398:  dependencies and write scope are the lane's.
399:- **Delivery.** This section reaches a lane through the re-read duty, not the driver's prompt
400:  template (one of five child-lane items): the integrator names the exact `lane_prompt()` addition
401:  in its round report, and closure grades no gate conformant until its registry row exists in the
402:  lane's own `SKILL.md`.
403:  The closure gate verifies the history pin (§Round-robin step 4) as committed evidence; a pin
404:  failure is a conformance defect routed under Closure consequence.
405:
406:## File contract per shokunin repo
407:
408:| File | Purpose |
409:|---|---|
410:| `SKILL.md` | The specialist's craft: triggers, decision tables, error patterns, checklists, cited sources. Its frontmatter `description` carries quoted trigger strings, an anti-trigger, and a sibling-arbitration note — capability-and-scope-only descriptions misroute |
411:| `PROVINCE.md` | Domain boundary: what it owns, what it refuses, its work surfaces. Declared surfaces must resolve; when a lane finds a surface moved or absent it corrects `PROVINCE.md` to the real path and logs the correction |
412:| `LOG.md` | Append-only iteration log: round entries, accepted changes, falsifiable next-iterations |
413:| `SHONEN.md` | Promotion checklist to shokunin; generated at mint by copying the canonical template (below) verbatim and deleted on promotion. Gates evolve — when they change, the owning lane regenerates `SHONEN.md` verbatim from the template on its next steered round (the lane is the only allowed writer inside its repo). Verification is mechanical: the seed block (indented lines below) must diff byte-identical modulo `<name>` = the repo's directory name, and marks are confined to the box character plus one indented evidence line per box — `[x] <verifier-id>` or `[~]` with a resolvable pointer; no other prose, added boxes, or removed boxes (§Appendix, "Canonical form") |
414:| `AGENTS.md` | Operating rules when working inside this repo |
415:| `corpus/` | Proprietary knowledge corpus per `CORPUS.md`: `README.md` index, `knowledge/` sourced domain notes, `lessons/` per-round training lessons; reviewed by the aggregator lane every round |
416:| `SCORECARD.md` | Axis scores per `AXES.md`: owned axes → score 0–10 → evidence pointer → last-change round, plus `planned` and `retired`. Every score is a claim: it carries the counting command that produced it and the commit it was measured against, so a reader can re-derive it |
417:| `PROTOCOL-APPENDIX.md` | Main repo, protocol-lane owned: the incident digest that motivates `PROTOCOL.md`'s rules, and a REQUIRED sibling input for appendix-pointer verification. Rows are append-only dated incidents; the body's `(§Appendix, "X")` pointers resolve to the row whose first column names `X` |
418:
419:The canonical `SHONEN.md` seed (verbatim — `<name>` is the only substitution):
420:
421:    # <name> — Promotion checklist
422:
423:    Promotion to shokunin requires all of:
424:
425:    - [ ] SKILL.md contains real decision tables, error patterns, checklists, cited sources
426:    - [ ] At least one end-to-end domain task executed and logged in LOG.md
427:    - [ ] Instructions executable by an agent without oral context
428:    - [ ] No cross-domain bleed (PROVINCE.md still accurate)
429:
430:Marks: `[~]` asserted by the lane itself (evidence pointer required), `[x]` only with a named
431:non-author verifier per **Promotion gates**.
432:
433:## Invariants
434:
435:- Specialize, don't generalize: a shokunin's `SKILL.md` contains *cited, verifiable* knowledge of
436:  its domain — never generic agent advice.
437:- One domain per shokunin; a domain belongs to one shokunin. Contested scope — evidence or work
438:  is reported in the lane report; the integrator arbitrates by refining `PROVINCE.md` and records
439:  the ruling in the round notes. A contested-scope report left unruled by the next completed round
440:  is re-flagged in the lane report, the round notes, and an open aggregator-ledger row;
441:  silence is not a ruling and must never default scope to whichever lane wrote first.
442:- Rounds are evidence-driven: every `LOG.md` entry cites the work that motivated it.
443:- `LOG.md` is append-only: entries are never rewritten or deleted; corrections land as new entries.
444:- `MANIFEST.json` is canonical for rank and roster; `ROADMAP.md` mirrors it. Only integrator roles
445:  write main-repo files: `MISSION.md`, `AXES.md`, `CORPUS.md`, and `scripts/` are operator-side integrator files,
446:  whose corrections the protocol lane names in its round notes and does not edit; the protocol lane
447:  holds the `PROTOCOL.md`/`ROADMAP.md`/report writes plus, as integrator-of-record, `MANIFEST.json`
448:  `rounds` appends; edits *outside* `rounds` stay operator-side. Lanes write only inside their own
449:  child repo and their lane report at `.ufo/reports/round-<N>/<id>.md`; the two main-repo lanes
450:  (`protocol`, `aggregator`) also keep `SCORECARD.md` and `LOG.md` at the main-repo root.
451:  `.ufo/reports/`, `.ufo/waves/`, and the round's `.ufo/prompts/*.md` are committed with the round's
452:  integration commit — an untracked prompt is non-durable dispatch evidence. `.ufo/state/` and
453:  `.ufo/watchdog.log` are driver runtime that churns every tick, tracked since `609ecb6` (§Appendix, "Tracked runtime"); no lane commit
454:  may include them — pathspec-limited commits are the enforcement, and untracking them is operator-side
455:  work named in the round notes.
456:- A meta-domain shokunin (e.g. prompt & skill craft) documents *patterns*; it does
457:  not own the protocol files, other provinces' files, or promotions.
458:- Local-first: repos live locally; **domain-facing actions are operator-owned** (publishing, vault
459:  approval, claim submission). Push scope is owned by `MISSION.md` §Push scope — hard rule (operator
460:  rule, landed in `235b414` 2026-09-28): lanes push only to the main repo and their own
461:  `<lane>-shokunin` remote; domain source trees are read-only and upstream-bound work rides the
462:  round report. Repo bookkeeping — committing and `git push`ing the round's commits — is ordinary
463:  lane work, not publishing, when the driver instructs it. Exception: operator-gated artifacts
464:  (staged payloads, publish candidates, vault request material, evidence under embargo) are
465:  committed locally but not pushed until the operator releases the gate — bookkeeping never
466:  front-runs an operator decision. A lane's main-repo commit is pathspec-limited to its own report
467:  file (`git commit -- .ufo/reports/round-<N>/<id>.md`) — never `commit -a` / `add -A`, which sweeps
468:  up sibling in-flight edits and integrator working-tree changes.
469:- Lane authorship is auditable: each child repo is configured at mint so round commits carry the
470:  lane identity (`<lane>-shokunin` / `<lane>@shokunin.local`). A lane finding its repo unconfigured
471:  sets `git config user.name/email` once and notes it in `LOG.md`; commits under the operator
472:  identity made by lane rounds are a conformance defect (§Appendix, "Lane identity"). Main-repo
473:  commits follow the same rule but cannot rely on `git config`, the shared main-repo identity being
474:  the operator's personal one: a main-repo lane commits with `git -c user.name=<lane>-shokunin -c
475:  user.email=<lane>@shokunin.local commit …`.
476:- `corpus/` inherits the evidence standard: every `knowledge/` entry cites a resolvable source;
477:  `corpus/lessons/` entries cite the round and its LOG.md entry or lane report. Corpus corrections
478:  are new entries, never in-place rewrites: no lane edits another lane's corpus files, and
479:  `round-<N>-aggregator-*.md` are aggregator-owned.
480:
481:## Fleet-2 conventions (adopted)
482:
483:- Expertise axes live in `AXES.md`; each lane owns a named subset and works one axis-move per round,
484:  measured in `SCORECARD.md`. An axis-move inherits the evidence standard: before and after numbers
485:  each carry the counting command and the commit they were measured against, and a score no reader
486:  can re-derive is an opinion, not a measurement. A `SCORECARD.md` axis name not defined in
487:  `AXES.md` (`novelty`, `consistency`) is worked only if its row carries its mapping to one of the
488:  six axes `AXES.md` defines, in the same row, so a non-author can re-derive it. Axis work does not
489:  displace the file contract — a round that moves an axis while `corpus/`, `LOG.md`, or `SHONEN.md`
490:  drift is a conformance defect like any other.
491:- `MISSION.md` is the mission SSOT: fleet shape, model route table, concurrency floor (the L2
492:  minimum's source), push rule, L0 side channel. Watchdog prompts bind to it. Precedence between the
493:  two SSOTs: `PROTOCOL.md` owns process, evidence, and gates; where they conflict on process —
494:  `MISSION.md`'s unconditional "commit then push" against this file's operator-gated hold —
495:  `PROTOCOL.md` wins and the conflict is named in the round notes; neither file is edited by a lane.
496:- L0 side channel: lanes append `.ufo/l0-questions.md`; the aggregator surfaces it. The file is
497:  append-only — a lane restating or correcting its own question
498:  appends a new line naming the superseded one and never rewrites a filed line, and the operator's
499:  in-place answers are never a lane write. Cite a question by lane + round + its opening words,
500:  never by line number: the queue grows, so every line number moves. Its durability owner is the
501:  integrator, which commits it with the round's integration commit — a lane's appended question is
502:  non-durable until committed and no lane owns the path (§Appendix, "L0 durability").

504:## Appendix — incident digest (why these rules exist)

The **aggregator** lane is a main-repo lane that reviews every child repo's `corpus/` each round
(per `CORPUS.md`), files gaps as lessons inside the child repos, and files its own round report at
`.ufo/reports/round-<N>/aggregator.md`. Its report covers per-repo corpus verdicts and cross-lane
learnings. It is the sole exception to lane write-scope: it may create or repair `corpus/` inside any
child repo, and nothing else — no main-repo files outside its own report and ledger. Every file it
creates inside a child repo is **committed by the aggregator itself at creation time**, pathspec-limited
to its own files, under its own subject (`corpus: round-<N> aggregator …`) — never left uncommitted for
a lane's round commit to sweep, and a lane never commits an aggregator-owned file. Alongside the
per-round report it maintains one rolling audit ledger — canonically `.ufo/reports/AGGREGATE.md`,
and no third path counts; a superseded
snapshot elsewhere is relocated there by its next refresh and remains readable evidence, superseded
and not voided. While the canonical ledger is absent or unrefreshed, the integrator's round notes
are the queue of record (§Appendix, "Ledger"). The ledger is append-only in the same sense as
`LOG.md` — refresh sections supersede earlier rows explicitly rather than rewriting them. An
aggregator round report is incomplete unless the ledger was refreshed or the report names why no row
changed. A round filed without the ledger duty keeps the routed-defect queue empty by construction.

## Evidence standard

Everywhere the protocol says *evidence*, it means a resolvable pointer: a repo path, a command and
its output, a commit, or an external document — never a naked assertion. A `LOG.md` entry without a
pointer is not evidence; an unreachable claim in a lane report does not exist.
An **end-to-end domain task** is one real work item executed against the domain's actual surfaces,
logged as trigger → action → outcome → pointer. Where the domain's terminal action is operator-owned
(§Invariants, local-first), executed means *prepared + verified + handed off*: the handoff artifact
is the outcome pointer, and a documented negative result at that gate still counts.
A numeric claim carries its counting command, an absence claim its search sweep, and a quote its
location (frontmatter/body, file, line) — the `CORPUS.md` rules bind `LOG.md` entries and lane
reports too, not only `corpus/`. A status command printing configured values is not evidence of
capability: endpoint/ability claims need a probe against the real surface.
An evidence pointer must resolve at *closure* time, not only at write time: paths under `tmpfs`
(`/tmp`, `/dev/shm`), session-scoped `local://` artifacts, and any pointer a fresh session cannot
reach are not evidence — commit the artifact or cite a reproducible command. A timestamp on evidence
must be at or before the commit that ships it — future-dated evidence is a conformance defect
(§Appendix, "Evidence standard").
- **Claimed ≠ re-executed.** A command offered as evidence is a re-run performed at write time with
  its observed output — never an output quoted from memory or a prior session.
- **Corrections sweep every mention.** Before a round's commit, grep every file the lane touches
  (`corpus/README.md`, `SKILL.md`, `knowledge/`) for the superseded claim — a corrected fact left
  standing in a sibling file is still a defect.
- **A falsified claim in an append-only file gets a named correction entry in the lane's next
  round** — appended, never rewritten; it stays on the routed-defect queue until it lands.
- **Commits are cited by hash, never by subject or tag** — `git rev-parse round-4` fails wherever
  the tag doesn't exist.
- **Drift pins.** A pin counts only if its expected values are **persisted inside the repo** (a
  recorded sha/mode/lines baseline, or a committed expected-output file the script diffs against); a
  fingerprint *printer* with no stored baseline cannot detect drift; a pin is `RECOMMENDED` where the
  cited surface is outside the lane's control.

## Gate standard

A **gate** is a committed, re-runnable verdict script a lane owns: it reads surfaces, compares them
against expected values persisted in its own repo, and returns a verdict. A tool that cannot fail is
a **probe**, and is registered as one.
- **Verdict.** `0` = `clean` and `1` = `failed` fleet-wide; every other code a gate exits (`2`, `3`,
  `64`, …) is declared in its registry entry and mapped onto `clean | failed | could-not-evaluate`,
  and an undeclared nonzero code reads as `could-not-evaluate`. Nothing else is pinned: a gate's own
  vocabulary — WARN vs HIT, a missing baseline, finding kinds — stays lane-owned, and this section
  governs the outer interface only.
- **Self-test.** Every gate exposes a self-invocation mode over isolated fixtures (temp trees, no
  network, no live-tree write) asserting both the exit code and a stable expected finding-id, with
  the expected values committed in the owning repo and independent of the recomputation. The flag
  spelling is the lane's (`--selftest`, `--self-test`, `run_selftest()`)
  and the registry records it; a helper-only or model-only self-check does not satisfy this clause.
- **Two evidences.** Self-test green is capability, not a measurement (§Evidence standard). A gate
  whose verdict depends on a mutable fleet artifact also ships a run over a committed input snapshot
  with its committed expected verdict, so a later hand-edit of that artifact contradicts the frozen
  run. A verdict names the revision it was measured against: a gate grades the tree it runs on, so a
  run over a moving worktree is not comparable to one over the cited commit. A frozen baseline's
  `expected.json` MUST pin the digest of every snapshot input file, and the gate verifies those
  digests before comparing verdicts: an edited snapshot is `snapshot_tampered` (could-not-evaluate),
  not a compared verdict, and a baseline without digests is reported `unpinned (legacy)`.
- **Registry.** The schema is this section's; the rows live in each lane's `SKILL.md`: name,
  `gate|probe`, entry command, verdict map (code → class), self-test command and spelling,
  pinned-value path, write scope, owner. The aggregator ledger stays the routed-defect queue, not a
  second inventory; a fleet index is pointers to lane rows, never copied expected values. Frozen
  baseline names resolve under any `.ufo/waves/*/frozen` root; a bare name matching more than one
  root fails closed.
- **Scope.** Read-only over surfaces it does not own, and it never acts on an external surface —
  publishing, vault approval, claim submission and driver mutation stay operator-owned (§Invariants,
  local-first). A verdict is lane-local evidence: it
  never defines the host runtime's stop conditions (`loop_stop`/`mission_goal`) and
  never stands in for the native judge.
- **Closure consequence.** A red gate is a conformance defect recorded in the round notes and routed
  to its owner — status-neutral unless the round's rules already prescribe `failed`; gate redness is
  never the marker predicate, since step 1 grades marker-versus-real-report first and only a marker
  invokes `failed`. The integrator verifies a gate's *committed evidence* (self-test tally,
  frozen-run verdict, the revision measured); it does not execute a sibling's gate, whose
  dependencies and write scope are the lane's.
- **Delivery.** This section reaches a lane through the re-read duty, not the driver's prompt
  template (one of five child-lane items): the integrator names the exact `lane_prompt()` addition
  in its round report, and closure grades no gate conformant until its registry row exists in the
  lane's own `SKILL.md`.
  The closure gate verifies the history pin (§Round-robin step 4) as committed evidence; a pin
  failure is a conformance defect routed under Closure consequence.

## File contract per shokunin repo

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `SKILL.md` | The specialist's craft: triggers, decision tables, error patterns, checklists, cited sources. Its frontmatter `description` carries quoted trigger strings, an anti-trigger, and a sibling-arbitration note — capability-and-scope-only descriptions misroute |
| `PROVINCE.md` | Domain boundary: what it owns, what it refuses, its work surfaces. Declared surfaces must resolve; when a lane finds a surface moved or absent it corrects `PROVINCE.md` to the real path and logs the correction |
| `LOG.md` | Append-only iteration log: round entries, accepted changes, falsifiable next-iterations |
| `SHONEN.md` | Promotion checklist to shokunin; generated at mint by copying the canonical template (below) verbatim and deleted on promotion. Gates evolve — when they change, the owning lane regenerates `SHONEN.md` verbatim from the template on its next steered round (the lane is the only allowed writer inside its repo). Verification is mechanical: the seed block (indented lines below) must diff byte-identical modulo `<name>` = the repo's directory name, and marks are confined to the box character plus one indented evidence line per box — `[x] <verifier-id>` or `[~]` with a resolvable pointer; no other prose, added boxes, or removed boxes (§Appendix, "Canonical form") |
| `AGENTS.md` | Operating rules when working inside this repo |
| `corpus/` | Proprietary knowledge corpus per `CORPUS.md`: `README.md` index, `knowledge/` sourced domain notes, `lessons/` per-round training lessons; reviewed by the aggregator lane every round |
| `SCORECARD.md` | Axis scores per `AXES.md`: owned axes → score 0–10 → evidence pointer → last-change round, plus `planned` and `retired`. Every score is a claim: it carries the counting command that produced it and the commit it was measured against, so a reader can re-derive it |
| `PROTOCOL-APPENDIX.md` | Main repo, protocol-lane owned: the incident digest that motivates `PROTOCOL.md`'s rules, and a REQUIRED sibling input for appendix-pointer verification. Rows are append-only dated incidents; the body's `(§Appendix, "X")` pointers resolve to the row whose first column names `X` |

The canonical `SHONEN.md` seed (verbatim — `<name>` is the only substitution):

    # <name> — Promotion checklist

    Promotion to shokunin requires all of:

    - [ ] SKILL.md contains real decision tables, error patterns, checklists, cited sources
    - [ ] At least one end-to-end domain task executed and logged in LOG.md
    - [ ] Instructions executable by an agent without oral context
    - [ ] No cross-domain bleed (PROVINCE.md still accurate)

Marks: `[~]` asserted by the lane itself (evidence pointer required), `[x]` only with a named
non-author verifier per **Promotion gates**.

## Invariants

- Specialize, don't generalize: a shokunin's `SKILL.md` contains *cited, verifiable* knowledge of
  its domain — never generic agent advice.
- One domain per shokunin; a domain belongs to one shokunin. Contested scope — evidence or work
  is reported in the lane report; the integrator arbitrates by refining `PROVINCE.md` and records
  the ruling in the round notes. A contested-scope report left unruled by the next completed round
  is re-flagged in the lane report, the round notes, and an open aggregator-ledger row;
  silence is not a ruling and must never default scope to whichever lane wrote first.
- Rounds are evidence-driven: every `LOG.md` entry cites the work that motivated it.
- `LOG.md` is append-only: entries are never rewritten or deleted; corrections land as new entries.
- `MANIFEST.json` is canonical for rank and roster; `ROADMAP.md` mirrors it. Only integrator roles
  write main-repo files: `MISSION.md`, `AXES.md`, `CORPUS.md`, and `scripts/` are operator-side integrator files,
  whose corrections the protocol lane names in its round notes and does not edit; the protocol lane
  holds the `PROTOCOL.md`/`ROADMAP.md`/report writes plus, as integrator-of-record, `MANIFEST.json`
  `rounds` appends; edits *outside* `rounds` stay operator-side. Lanes write only inside their own
  child repo and their lane report at `.ufo/reports/round-<N>/<id>.md`; the two main-repo lanes
  (`protocol`, `aggregator`) also keep `SCORECARD.md` and `LOG.md` at the main-repo root.
  `.ufo/reports/`, `.ufo/waves/`, and the round's `.ufo/prompts/*.md` are committed with the round's
  integration commit — an untracked prompt is non-durable dispatch evidence. `.ufo/state/` and
  `.ufo/watchdog.log` are driver runtime that churns every tick, tracked since `609ecb6` (§Appendix, "Tracked runtime"); no lane commit
  may include them — pathspec-limited commits are the enforcement, and untracking them is operator-side
  work named in the round notes.
- A meta-domain shokunin (e.g. prompt & skill craft) documents *patterns*; it does
  not own the protocol files, other provinces' files, or promotions.
- Local-first: repos live locally; **domain-facing actions are operator-owned** (publishing, vault
  approval, claim submission). Push scope is owned by `MISSION.md` §Push scope — hard rule (operator
  rule, landed in `235b414` 2026-09-28): lanes push only to the main repo and their own
  `<lane>-shokunin` remote; domain source trees are read-only and upstream-bound work rides the
  round report. Repo bookkeeping — committing and `git push`ing the round's commits — is ordinary
  lane work, not publishing, when the driver instructs it. Exception: operator-gated artifacts
  (staged payloads, publish candidates, vault request material, evidence under embargo) are
  committed locally but not pushed until the operator releases the gate — bookkeeping never
  front-runs an operator decision. A lane's main-repo commit is pathspec-limited to its own report
  file (`git commit -- .ufo/reports/round-<N>/<id>.md`) — never `commit -a` / `add -A`, which sweeps
  up sibling in-flight edits and integrator working-tree changes.
- Lane authorship is auditable: each child repo is configured at mint so round commits carry the
  lane identity (`<lane>-shokunin` / `<lane>@shokunin.local`). A lane finding its repo unconfigured
  sets `git config user.name/email` once and notes it in `LOG.md`; commits under the operator
  identity made by lane rounds are a conformance defect (§Appendix, "Lane identity"). Main-repo
  commits follow the same rule but cannot rely on `git config`, the shared main-repo identity being
  the operator's personal one: a main-repo lane commits with `git -c user.name=<lane>-shokunin -c
  user.email=<lane>@shokunin.local commit …`.
- `corpus/` inherits the evidence standard: every `knowledge/` entry cites a resolvable source;
  `corpus/lessons/` entries cite the round and its LOG.md entry or lane report. Corpus corrections
  are new entries, never in-place rewrites: no lane edits another lane's corpus files, and
  `round-<N>-aggregator-*.md` are aggregator-owned.

## Fleet-2 conventions (adopted)

- Expertise axes live in `AXES.md`; each lane owns a named subset and works one axis-move per round,
  measured in `SCORECARD.md`. An axis-move inherits the evidence standard: before and after numbers
  each carry the counting command and the commit they were measured against, and a score no reader
  can re-derive is an opinion, not a measurement. A `SCORECARD.md` axis name not defined in
  `AXES.md` (`novelty`, `consistency`) is worked only if its row carries its mapping to one of the
  six axes `AXES.md` defines, in the same row, so a non-author can re-derive it. Axis work does not
  displace the file contract — a round that moves an axis while `corpus/`, `LOG.md`, or `SHONEN.md`
  drift is a conformance defect like any other.
- `MISSION.md` is the mission SSOT: fleet shape, model route table, concurrency floor (the L2
  minimum's source), push rule, L0 side channel. Watchdog prompts bind to it. Precedence between the
  two SSOTs: `PROTOCOL.md` owns process, evidence, and gates; where they conflict on process —
  `MISSION.md`'s unconditional "commit then push" against this file's operator-gated hold —
  `PROTOCOL.md` wins and the conflict is named in the round notes; neither file is edited by a lane.
- L0 side channel: lanes append `.ufo/l0-questions.md`; the aggregator surfaces it. The file is
  append-only — a lane restating or correcting its own question
  appends a new line naming the superseded one and never rewrites a filed line, and the operator's
  in-place answers are never a lane write. Cite a question by lane + round + its opening words,
  never by line number: the queue grows, so every line number moves. Its durability owner is the
  integrator, which commits it with the round's integration commit — a lane's appended question is
  non-durable until committed and no lane owns the path (§Appendix, "L0 durability").

## Appendix — incident digest (why these rules exist)
The incident digest lives in the committed sibling artifact `PROTOCOL-APPENDIX.md` (repo root, protocol-lane owned); `PROTOCOL.md` and `PROTOCOL-APPENDIX.md` are a REQUIRED pair for reading and verification and a reader or protocol-pointer verifier fails closed if either is absent. `§Appendix` means that artifact's first-column rule key, never an in-body incident table, and every incident pointer in this file resolves to the row of that artifact whose first column names the quoted rule.

## 5. WWKD plan

```
fn wwkd_plan(state) -> Plan:
    1. data walk         — inspect cache, telemetry, and local diff first
    2. skeleton first    — establish one end-to-end shape before capacity
    3. overfit one case  — prove one concrete path, then generalize one axis
    4. cheapest local check — use pattern checks before expensive local work
    5. verification gate — every milestone names its observable check
    6. least disruption  — order moves so each remains runnable in isolation
```

The plan is written by the one L1. A planner card may provide advice on hosts
that support it, but it never becomes a second judge or runtime. The WWKD
posture is uncapped on milestones; the plan artifact itself is read under
`MAX_PLAN_ARTIFACT_BYTES` (4 MiB, loop_driver.rs:112).

Every declared axis names its measurement (`Axis.measurement`, declared with
the round's axis set): `executable` axes are measured by the runtime
— the check runs in a bounded scratch copy of the baseline tree and of
the candidate tree (the proposal's declared `candidate_writes`), never
the live tree, and the judge consumes the computed direction-aware delta;
seat scores on an executable axis are advisory context and never override
a computed regression. `subjective` axes admit a claimed improvement only
through the recorded symmetric argument (for and against sides citing
role-appropriate evidence); one-sided claims are clamped to baseline and
flagged. `evidence` axes are computed by the judge from typed handoff
evidence and exist only on the native path — the fixture loop cannot
produce them and the native path cannot execute subprocess checks, so
each side rejects the other's kind at admission. A check that fails to
run measures UNKNOWN: never regression cover, never a phantom gain, and
UNKNOWN on a material axis blocks admission as `INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE`.
An axis with no measurement declaration fails the round's plan admission:
unmeasurable axes are not axes (verification-gate stance applied to the axis
set itself).
The verdict and round report carry the computed measurements and flags
as provenance.

156:  are positional `{path, address}` — schema properties are not flags

173:  171 (`corpus/knowledge/2026-10-13-r8-01-queue-a-ops.md:247-275`), lines
174:  181–183 and 187 (`corpus/knowledge/2026-10-14-r10-02-queue-ops-2.md:25-60`),

177:  (`corpus/knowledge/2026-10-13-r8-01-queue-a-ops.md:262-265`); the drain

179:  (`corpus/knowledge/2026-10-14-r12-01-queue-b-ready.md:1`); later-held
180:  Queue-B rows that postdated the census were bookkeeping lag, not
181:  wrong-at-write defects
182:  (`corpus/knowledge/2026-10-14-r12-01-queue-b-ready.md:105-108`).
183:- **Provisioning hints can be wrong — verify the gate, not the hint.** The
184:  census's `chromium --log-net-log` hint refuses typed against a real netlog;
185:  the operative gate is a har-schema-valid capture (playwright `recordHar`
186:  satisfies it) (`corpus/knowledge/2026-10-14-r10-01-queue-ops.md:138-142`).
187:  Same class: an env gate invisible in the capability matrix — census gates
188:  can be incomplete in BOTH directions
189:  (`corpus/knowledge/2026-10-14-r11-01-queue-ops.md:72-74`) — and the
190:  pwntools "one-fix" that is really the pin `setuptools<81`
191:  (`corpus/knowledge/2026-10-14-r12-01-queue-b-ready.md:23`).

193:## Checklists
194:
195:**Before any claim of "held":** carrier ran this round? evidence_id or
196:reproducing call cited? providers `status` (not per-op `available`)? versions
197:pinned (rea-agents@6.4.0, Ghidra 12.1.4, JDK 21)?
198:
199:**Before "empty/clean" claims:** parsed-and-empty vs excluded-from-inventory?
200:(`parse_failures:0` on unparsed members means nothing — typora lesson.)
201:Callers via objdump? GOT-indirect calls invisible — use `xrefs`.
202:
203:## Known limits (r4)
204:
205:- `record_pairs`/`compare_functions` have no CLI verbs — domain/MCP only;
206:  `changed` needs ALL bundle members paired.
207:- MCP session retention is epoch-scoped; `evidence_links` pin records across
208:  targets; evidence ids are `f(content, path, params)` — deterministic on
209:  same-path re-runs, NOT path-independent (cite `subject.digest.sha256` for
210:  cross-path identity).
211:- Provider probes run under `prlimit` (e.g. wakaru `--as=1GiB`) — a standalone-
212:  working tool can still OOM in REA's spawn context. Bind native ELF binaries
213:  over node shims (`REA_WAKARU_COMMAND` → `@wakaru/cli-linux-x64/wakaru`).
214:- Positional-arg pattern extends: `recover-javascript-sources <file> <outdir>`
215:  (file not dir, output dir must be absent), `inspect-evm-interface <path>
216:  <encoding>`, `extract-artifact` ignores extra positionals silently.
217:- Ghidra startup timeout hits ~>40MB targets: raise `REA_GHIDRA_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS`.
218:- jq-shadow = verified upstream jq-1.8.2 (kimi-swarm install 2026-10-03) —
219:  do not re-flag.
220:
221:## Refuses
222:
223:Malware triage at scale, non-REA dynamic analysis (gdb scripting, strace,
224:Frida), source-repo reconstruction, all engine/tooling installs, and
225:safety/quality verdicts on findings (Adjacent — report to orchestrator, never
226:absorb; PROVINCE.md). Boundary: "what does this shipped artifact do, per
227:evidence id X" — never "is it safe or trustworthy".

  `corpus/knowledge/2026-10-14-r11-01-queue-ops.md:212-217`); and
  `compare-managed-members` mints internal member ids that differ from CLI
  ids at identical bytes
  (`corpus/knowledge/2026-10-14-r10-01-queue-ops.md:89-96`). Establish the
  family first, then verify byte-exact (content-addressed) or run-normalized
  (per-run) accordingly
  (`corpus/knowledge/2026-10-14-r12-01-queue-b-ready.md:5`).
- **Raw file vaddrs must be pre-shifted +0x100000 into Ghidra space for every
  native verb on ELF PIE/DYN.** Proven on an executable (`/usr/bin/jq`,
  `corpus/knowledge/2026-10-13-r5-02-call-targets-jq.md:144-146`) and on
  shared objects (libjq
  `corpus/knowledge/2026-10-13-r7-01-queue-a-ops.md:174-177`; glibc `setenv`
  and libgtk `gtk_button_new`
  `corpus/knowledge/2026-10-14-r9-02-queue-a-ops-2.md:268-272`). An unshifted
  address is answered honestly, never decoded as garbage: typed
  `outside-memory`, exit 0, null bytes
  (`corpus/knowledge/2026-10-13-r7-02-queue-a-ops-2.md:47-60`).
- **Refusal families and cost classes.** `VALIDATION_ERROR` = zod
  fieldErrors, pre-analysis ~0.7 s
  (`corpus/knowledge/2026-10-13-r5-02-call-targets-jq.md:25-51`);
  `invalid_request` = semantic, in BOTH cost classes — pre-analysis 0.7 s on
  argument exclusivity
  (`corpus/knowledge/2026-10-13-r7-01-queue-a-ops.md:93-119`) but
  post-analysis ~14.2 s after a full import when a name must resolve against
  the analyzed program
  (`corpus/knowledge/2026-10-13-r8-01-queue-a-ops.md:118-134`);
  `capability_unavailable` = env gates such as `REA_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE`,
  invisible in the capabilities matrix
  (`corpus/knowledge/2026-10-14-r11-01-queue-ops.md:63-74`);
  `provider_unavailable` = missing engines / clean environment
  (`corpus/knowledge/2026-10-13-r5-01-riscv-bypass.md:78`,
  `corpus/knowledge/2026-10-14-r12-01-queue-b-ready.md:24`). `retryable`
  marks transport retryability, not arg-fixability
  (`corpus/knowledge/2026-10-13-r7-01-queue-a-ops.md:117-119`), and refusal
  latency is not a validity signal
  (`corpus/knowledge/2026-10-13-r8-01-queue-a-ops.md:130-132`).
- **Four authority grades — cite a conclusion at the grade its envelope
  declares.** `observed`+`shipped-artifact`: provider observation of the
  pinned artifact bytes
  (`corpus/knowledge/2026-10-13-r5-02-call-targets-jq.md:55-57`);
  `inferred`+`analyst-inference`: derived analytics over an authenticated
  input, citable as inference never as artifact observation
  (`corpus/knowledge/2026-10-13-r8-02-queue-a-ops-2.md:78-90`) and never
  promoted to exact identity
  (`corpus/knowledge/2026-10-14-r12-02-queue-b-ledger.md:53-54`);
  `observed`+`historical-reference`: retained producer evidence without
  execution attribution — "Recorded URLs are never fetched"
  (`corpus/knowledge/2026-10-14-r10-01-queue-ops.md:166-173`);
  `observed`+`controlled-replay`: scripted pty replay with residual unknowns
  stated (`corpus/knowledge/2026-10-14-r11-01-queue-ops.md:197-207`).
- **Input contracts are shape-gated.** Ledger/coverage verbs consume a
  canonically wrapped Evidence bundle — hand-wrapped manifests refuse "not
  canonical"; wrap with the package's own `createEvidenceBundle`
  (`corpus/knowledge/2026-10-14-r9-01-queue-a-ops.md:41-48`). The
  application-graph projectors take a homogeneous `inspect_artifact`-only
  inventory — keyed-archive/IB evidences are schema-valid yet
  workflow-refused, and the same refusal string and law hold for Android
  (`corpus/knowledge/2026-10-14-r11-02-queue-ops-2.md:51-65`,
  `corpus/knowledge/2026-10-14-r12-01-queue-b-ready.md:50`). Native CLI verbs
  are positional `{path, address}` — schema properties are not flags
  (`corpus/knowledge/2026-10-13-r5-02-call-targets-jq.md:36-41`).
- **Module attribution is caller-attested, not proven.** `analyze_function`
  ids hash content+parameters, not the path: the same glibc bytes under a
  renamed path flip one P/Invoke verdict `contradicted`→`verified`
  (`corpus/knowledge/2026-10-14-r9-02-queue-a-ops-2.md:106-141`), and a
  subject-only rewrite reproduces the renamed-path envelope bit-for-bit at
  the same id — verdicts attest the analysis, callers attest the module; pin
  request bytes when module identity matters
  (`corpus/knowledge/2026-10-14-r9-02-queue-a-ops-2.md:146-169`).
- **Tool acceptance ≠ correctness.** `trace-web-source-location`'s VLQ
  validator catches dangling continuations yet accepted a semantically wrong
  line-delta map; the defect surfaced only via an independent decoder — never
  treat a pass as input correctness; cross-check independently
  (`corpus/knowledge/2026-10-14-r11-01-queue-ops.md:123-129`, run log :311).
- **Census rows can be defects — check holdings before exercising.** Six
  recorded instances of rows queued while already held: row 7 / table line
  171 (`corpus/knowledge/2026-10-13-r8-01-queue-a-ops.md:247-275`), lines
  181–183 and 187 (`corpus/knowledge/2026-10-14-r10-02-queue-ops-2.md:25-60`),
  L195 (`corpus/knowledge/2026-10-14-r12-02-queue-b-ledger.md:161-166`,
  "sixth instance"). Same-round wave entries count as exercised
  (`corpus/knowledge/2026-10-13-r8-01-queue-a-ops.md:262-265`); the drain
  move is a holdings pre-check with re-derivation, "do not re-exercise"
  (`corpus/knowledge/2026-10-14-r12-01-queue-b-ready.md:1`); later-held
  Queue-B rows that postdated the census were bookkeeping lag, not
  wrong-at-write defects
  (`corpus/knowledge/2026-10-14-r12-01-queue-b-ready.md:105-108`).
- **Provisioning hints can be wrong — verify the gate, not the hint.** The
  census's `chromium --log-net-log` hint refuses typed against a real netlog;
  the operative gate is a har-schema-valid capture (playwright `recordHar`
  satisfies it) (`corpus/knowledge/2026-10-14-r10-01-queue-ops.md:138-142`).
  Same class: an env gate invisible in the capability matrix — census gates
  can be incomplete in BOTH directions
  (`corpus/knowledge/2026-10-14-r11-01-queue-ops.md:72-74`) — and the
  pwntools "one-fix" that is really the pin `setuptools<81`
  (`corpus/knowledge/2026-10-14-r12-01-queue-b-ready.md:23`).

## Checklists

**Before any claim of "held":** carrier ran this round? evidence_id or
reproducing call cited? providers `status` (not per-op `available`)? versions
pinned (rea-agents@6.4.0, Ghidra 12.1.4, JDK 21)?

**Before "empty/clean" claims:** parsed-and-empty vs excluded-from-inventory?
(`parse_failures:0` on unparsed members means nothing — typora lesson.)
Callers via objdump? GOT-indirect calls invisible — use `xrefs`.

## Known limits (r4)

- `record_pairs`/`compare_functions` have no CLI verbs — domain/MCP only;
  `changed` needs ALL bundle members paired.
- MCP session retention is epoch-scoped; `evidence_links` pin records across
  targets; evidence ids are `f(content, path, params)` — deterministic on
  same-path re-runs, NOT path-independent (cite `subject.digest.sha256` for
  cross-path identity).
- Provider probes run under `prlimit` (e.g. wakaru `--as=1GiB`) — a standalone-
  working tool can still OOM in REA's spawn context. Bind native ELF binaries
  over node shims (`REA_WAKARU_COMMAND` → `@wakaru/cli-linux-x64/wakaru`).
- Positional-arg pattern extends: `recover-javascript-sources <file> <outdir>`
  (file not dir, output dir must be absent), `inspect-evm-interface <path>
  <encoding>`, `extract-artifact` ignores extra positionals silently.
- Ghidra startup timeout hits ~>40MB targets: raise `REA_GHIDRA_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS`.
- jq-shadow = verified upstream jq-1.8.2 (kimi-swarm install 2026-10-03) —
  do not re-flag.

## Refuses

Malware triage at scale, non-REA dynamic analysis (gdb scripting, strace,
Frida), source-repo reconstruction, all engine/tooling installs, and
safety/quality verdicts on findings (Adjacent — report to orchestrator, never
absorb; PROVINCE.md). Boundary: "what does this shipped artifact do, per
evidence id X" — never "is it safe or trustworthy".

5: * Ports the verified kimi-code `/swarm` (AgentSwarm) semantics onto OMP's
6: * `task` batch transport, per run-logic §4.3:

8: *   - ONE dispatch call per wave. The emitted `tasks` array is the payload of
9: *     a single batched `task` call; splitting it into several calls violates
10: *     the one-swarm-per-wave rule (kimi AgentSwarmExclusiveDenyPermissionPolicy).
11: *   - At most 100 lanes per wave, counting spawn items and resumes together:
12: *     the operator contract's global per-L1 atomized-L2 maximum, stricter
13: *     than kimi's MAX_AGENT_SWARM_SUBAGENTS=128. `sighting.dispatch.swarm.maxLanes`
14: *     and a per-spec `maxLanes` may only tighten the cap, never widen it.
15: *   - Wave band: a wave with spawn lanes carries waveMinLanes..waveMaxLanes
16: *     (config `sighting.dispatch.swarm.waveMinLanes`/`waveMaxLanes`, defaulting
17: *     to the swarm band); a resume-only wave may be a single lane
18: *     (kimi hasMinimumAgentSwarmInputs).
19: *   - `{{item}}` template expansion; pairwise-distinct expanded prompts are
20: *     REQUIRED — a duplicated expansion fails the wave before any lane
21: *     spawns (kimi Map-dedupe throw). Never dedupe silently.
22: *   - Resume preserves identity: a resume lane emits `{resume, message}` —
23: *     the OMP mapping is `hub send` / `handle.send` to the parked agent id,
24: *     which revives the same agent with its transcript and role. A resumed
25: *     lane never carries a new `role`/`agent` (that would mint a
26: *     replacement identity, violating I6).
27: *   - Every spawn lane carries an explicit taxonomy role — never a wave of
28: *     generic `task` agents. Swarm roles are the ten proposal roles;
29: *     planner/distiller/labrat/Main are frozen-topology seats, not swarm
30: *     lanes.

32: *     collapse is the lane role's pinned route resolved from the global OMP
33: *     alias table (AGENTS.md Routing authority) — never a hardcoded model.

36: * call. On OMP the single `task` call is the wave and the harness queues
37: * lanes beyond its concurrency window; the ramp constants are recorded in
38: * the plan as declared pacing policy for substrates that pace manually.
39: *
40: * CLI (operator surface — declare a wave inline instead of staging a JSON
41: * file; kimi's `/swarm` slash layer parses only `on|off|<prompt>`, so the
42: * inline-declaration port is the spec SOURCE, not a new argument grammar):
43: *   node scripts/ufo-swarm-wave.mjs plan --spec <wave.json|-> [--emit-tasks]
44: *   node scripts/ufo-swarm-wave.mjs plan --spec-json <json> [--emit-tasks]
45: *   node scripts/ufo-swarm-wave.mjs run  --spec <wave.json|->
46: *   node scripts/ufo-swarm-wave.mjs run  --spec-json <json>
47: *   node scripts/ufo-swarm-wave.mjs record --registry <path> --assignments <json>
48: *   --spec - reads spec JSON from stdin with the same fail-closed bound as
49: *   the file path. plan validates and emits the ufo-swarm-wave-v1 plan (or
50: *   only plan.tasks with --emit-tasks). run validates and emits
51: *   ufo-swarm-wave-dispatch-v1 — the exact single `task` call payload
52: *   ({context, tasks} — spawn lanes only, null when the wave resumes only)

55: *   reportDir/swarm-registry.json or .ufo/scopes/<wave>/swarm-registry.json:

61: *   requireOwnedSubagent parity). The registry also persists each member's

67: *     "context": "# Goal ...",            // optional batch-level task context
68: *                                         //   (defaults to a minimal
69: *                                         //   transport-shaped skeleton —
70: *                                         //   the task call requires a
71: *                                         //   string context)
72: *     "template": "Audit {{item}} ...",   // optional; requires per-item "item"
73: *     "hoist": true,                      // optional; template waves hoist the
74: *                                         //   shared template (placeholder
75: *                                         //   intact) into the batch context
76: *                                         //   when the total payload shrinks
77: *                                         //   by >= MIN_HOIST_SAVINGS bytes;
78: *                                         //   ineligible/uneconomic waves
79: *                                         //   bypass with the reason recorded
80: *                                         //   in plan.compaction (r13)
81: *     "reportDir": ".ufo/scopes/x/recon", // optional per-lane report dir
82: *     "maxLanes": 32,                     // optional per-mission tightening
83: *     "priorRegistry": ".ufo/scopes/recon-0/swarm-registry.json", // optional
84: *     //   predecessor registry path (or array) a resume lane may name
85: *     "items": [
86: *       { "item": "src/auth", "role": "scout" },
87: *       { "prompt": "Review ...", "role": "reviewer", "name": "SwarmAudit" },
88: *       { "resume": "agent-abc123", "message": "Continue with ..." }
89: *     ]

93: *   --route-families       record the wave's route families (distinct resolved
94: *                          primary+chain per lane role, from one fd-bound
95: *                          global-config snapshot) in plan.routePreflight;
96: *   --route-probe <exe>    also ping each distinct hop once through <exe>
97: *                          (scripts/ufo-route-preflight.mjs has the probe
98: *                          contract). A family with no reachable hop fails
99: *                          the wave with route_unreachable BEFORE the registry
100: *                          is persisted or any payload is emitted.
101: *
102: * Prior refinement (ONESHOT WO-4 Move B, opt-in, plan and run):
103: *   --prior-refinement <ledger> --expect-parent-run <runId>
104: *                          read the parent round's titles-only digest through
105: *                          the shipped read-successor path and append the
106: *                          bounded ufo-refinement-context-v1 block (<= 16
107: *                          entries, <= 1 KiB, delimited as untrusted data) to
108: *                          the shared wave context; plan.priorRefinement binds
109: *                          its sha256. A parent mismatch or invalid chain is
110: *                          prior_refinement_refused; overflow is rejected.
111: *
112: * Exit codes: 0 ok · 1 invalid spec/plan (JSON error on stderr) · 64 usage.
113: */
