# Shokunin Fleet Mission — Source of Truth (fleet-2)

Binding mission instruction for every L1 lane. Changes persist into
`scripts/shokunin-watchdog.sh` prompt generation and are relayed to live lanes
by steer.

## Fleet shape (declared config)

Lanes are declared in `shokunin.conf` at the fleet root — the driver reads the
config each tick; nothing is hardcoded in `scripts/shokunin-watchdog.sh`. Each
lane declaration carries `id`, `cwd` (a repo under `$SHOKUNIN_ROOT` — the two
main-repo lanes point at the fleet root itself), `route` (a route name resolved
through the host model route table, never a bare model alias), and `axes`
(owned axes per `AXES.md`). All L1 lanes dispatch on the `swe`-class route of
the host model route table.

Initial config (the upstream fleet's nine lanes, axes preserved):

```yaml
lanes:
  protocol:   { cwd: $SHOKUNIN_ROOT,   axes: "fleet-meta: protocol soundness, gate integrity" }
  aggregator: { cwd: $SHOKUNIN_ROOT,   axes: "cross-lane quality, mint/dormancy calls, corpus review" }
  kasegi:     { cwd: kasegi-shokunin/, axes: "depth + coverage (bounty/security research)" }
  kengaku:    { cwd: kengaku-shokunin/, axes: "novelty + calibration (LLM eval/research)" }
  kake:       { cwd: kake-shokunin/,   axes: "operability + freshness (web properties)" }
  kumitate:   { cwd: kumitate-shokunin/, axes: "operability + coverage (orchestration/tooling)" }
  kotoba:     { cwd: kotoba-shokunin/, axes: "depth + consistency (prompt/skill craft)" }
  kagi:       { cwd: kagi-shokunin/,   axes: "freshness + calibration (secrets/vault ops)" }
  kama:       { cwd: kama-shokunin/,   axes: "operability + freshness (local model serving/endpoints)" }
# every lane: route: swe   (resolved via the host model route table)
```

Round-robin across lanes; `respawn-per-round`: a round ends when
`.ufo/reports/round-<N>/<lane>.md` lands and passes the driver's content check
(`SHONEN` heading + minimum substance per `PROTOCOL.md`); watchdog completes the
mission and launches a fresh process for round N+1. Cap: 1024/lane. Tick: 450s.

## The axes framework

`AXES.md` defines the six expertise axes (depth, coverage, operability,
freshness, calibration, adjacency). A lane's round is **one axis-move**: pick
the lowest-scoring axis in `SCORECARD.md`, land one verifiable improvement,
measure it, record before→after in `SCORECARD.md`, log evidence in `LOG.md`.
Axes may be retired on saturation or split into sub-axes — recorded in
`SCORECARD.md` with the reason. Axis assignments in `shokunin.conf` are initial;
lanes may add/remove axes on evidence (falsifiable claim per move).

## L2 concurrency — required

Every L1 lane MUST dispatch **at least 8 L2 subagents per round**, in **one
batched AgentSwarm call** (the Kimi host surface) — one call carrying all lanes,
not a sequence of individual dispatches. Roles are expressed as lane roles and
routed through the host model route table (persisted globally in
`shokunin.conf` + the operator's route override file):

| Role class | Route bucket |
|---|---|
| planner, connector | heavy-reasoning route |
| executor, scribe, scout | fast-execution route |
| reviewer, critic, sentinel, revenger, labrat, mutation-tester, simplifier, distiller | economy route (fallback: fast-execution route) |

## Round prompt

Dispatch prompts are generated from the shipped ROUND-PROMPT template
(`templates/round-prompt.md`), which embeds the full round contract verbatim:
mission/axes binding, the axis-move rule, the L2 floor (≥8 lanes, one batched
AgentSwarm call), the report path with its required sections (the five
child-lane items), commit-then-push ordering, push scope, and the L0 side
channel. Prompt generation binds to this file; the closure step-1 fidelity
check grades each round's committed `.ufo/prompts/*.md` against the template.

## Round end

Commit inside the owning repo then `git push`. Reports: `.ufo/reports/round-<N>/<lane>.md` on the main repo, commit + push.

## Push scope — hard rule

Lanes push ONLY to the fleet repo (`$SHOKUNIN_ROOT`, remote operator-chosen) or
their own `<lane>-shokunin` remote. Domain source trees (operator-designated
read-only checkouts outside the fleet root) are read-only surfaces: never
commit there, never push to their remotes. Work that belongs upstream is
documented in the lane report; the operator owns those pushes.

## L0 side channel

The operator is reachable via `.ufo/l0-questions.md` in the fleet repo: append a
line `<lane> | round-<N> | <question or decision needed>`. The aggregator lane
surfaces entries each round; the L0 answers by editing the file in place.

---
name: reverse-engineer-anything
description: Reverse engineer native, managed, Electron/JavaScript, packaged, firmware, and browser targets with REA. Use shipped-artifact or requested runtime evidence to explain features, compare versions, decompile code, or guide a reconstruction. Skip REA for ordinary source-repository architecture analysis.
metadata:

  tool_count: 207

# REA

Use REA when a claim depends on a shipped binary or package, decompilation,
passive application runtime evidence, or comparison with
behavior not established by available source. For ordinary analysis of a
complete source repository, use normal repository tools and do not run REA
readiness or provider commands.

## Connect only when needed

Installing this skill supplies instructions; it does not register the REA MCP
server, install analysis engines, or add tools to an already-running agent.

If REA tools are available and their registration is not known to be stale,
proceed directly to the target. Do not run diagnostics or setup before every
investigation. Use the connected server's actual tool list and input schemas;
a skill installed from repository main may describe capabilities absent from
an older npm release. Keep complete inline Evidence when that server does not
advertise retained references.

If tools are absent, a call is blocked by the client, or a required provider is
unavailable, read [connection and recovery](references/connection-and-recovery.md).
Diagnose the observed blocker, continue useful supported work, and resume the
original task after repair. Client approval, shell PATH, registration and engine
availability have different remedies; avoid repeating setup for all of them.

1. Diagnose without changing REA or client configuration. `npx` may download
   the package and write to npm's cache. For Codex, run
   `npx -y rea-agents@6.5.0 doctor --client codex --json`. Substitute the current
   supported client: `claude_code`, `claude_desktop`, `codex`, `cursor`,
   `gemini_cli`, `windsurf`, `devin`, `opencode`, `antigravity`, `copilot_cli`,
   `commandcode`, `vscode`, `grok_build`, `omp`, or `grok_bot`. `grok_bot` has no local
   file registration: doctor reports the Grok Bot chat step, and setup does not
   write `mcp.json`. If the client is unknown, use `doctor --json` and
   inspect its registration results before choosing a setup scope.
2. Distinguish the reason. Missing, malformed, or stale registration needs a
   scoped configuration repair. An aligned registration with no tools in the
   active session needs a restart/reconnection; doctor cannot prove that the
   current agent has connected. A missing provider affects only tasks requiring
   that provider: static JavaScript inspection needs neither Hopper nor Ghidra,
   and Android inspection has separate bring-your-own JADX/Java prerequisites.
3. For a configuration repair, prepare the read-only plan:
   `npx -y rea-agents@6.5.0 setup --client codex --dry-run --json`.
   Use the current client's ID, show its exact proposed paths, backups, and
   changes, and obtain approval before setup writes configuration or installs
   Hopper. Setup normally installs the matching bundled skill too; include that
   replacement in the reviewed plan. After approval, apply the same scope with
   `npx -y rea-agents@6.5.0 setup --client codex --yes`. Add `--install-hopper`
   only if that separate installation was needed and explicitly approved.
4. Restart/reconnect the affected agent. Verify that REA tools actually appear
   in the session, then resume the original investigation. If they remain
   absent, inspect the client's MCP launch error rather than repeating setup.

REA setup never installs or upgrades Node.js, npm, Homebrew, Java, Ghidra, IDA,
JADX, Binwalk, or Unblob. Use existing prerequisites; do not install unrelated
software to repair
MCP registration. For an unsupported client, use manual stdio registration
with a version-pinned `rea-agents` package or continue through the CLI.

A concrete CLI fallback for an operator-supplied JavaScript tree or ASAR is:

```bash
npx -y rea-agents@6.5.0 analyze-javascript-application /absolute/path/to/app --json
```

No MCP registration or native engine is required. Read the returned Evidence,
graph, limitations, and unknowns with the same care as an MCP result; the CLI
returns the Evidence record directly. This fallback does not establish that
MCP is configured. Native CLI tasks still require their selected engine.
Prefer an existing `rea` CLI. When none is installed and REA package acquisition
is within the authorized scope, use `npx -y rea-agents@6.5.0` in its place.
Configuration repair starts with a read-only setup plan; show paths, backups and
skill replacement before applying authorized changes. Preserve existing approval
and target-execution boundaries. REA setup never installs or upgrades unrelated
software, including Node.js, npm, Homebrew, Java, Ghidra, IDA, JADX, Binwalk or Unblob.

## Route the target first

Choose the first tool from the target the user supplied. Use `open_binary` for
active-target native or archive workflows; target-free tools take their own
explicit path or endpoint and do not need it.

- ASAR or extracted JavaScript/Electron tree:
  `analyze_javascript_application`.
- Archive/package member inventory (ZIP/APK/IPA/MSIX/AppX or DMG):
  `open_binary` with the supplied local path; use `inspect_artifact` when its
  graph and findings help answer the question.
- Android APK code, classes, methods, or incoming references:
  `inspect_android_package`, then focused Android tools when advertised.
  Archive member inventory still uses the archive route above.
- Managed PE/CLI assembly: `inspect_managed_artifact`.
- Firmware image: `inspect_firmware_regions` when advertised. Use
  `extract_firmware` when extraction is requested, with a caller-selected new
  absolute output directory. These tools use caller-supplied Binwalk/Unblob on
  Linux; see the [firmware guide](https://github.com/morluto/rea/blob/main/docs/firmware-analysis.md).
- .NET NativeAOT PE/ELF: native Ghidra analysis. Native code can yield pseudocode;
  consult the NativeAOT workflow in `references/native-and-artifacts.md` for
  optional metadata recovery and its supported host/layout boundary.
- User-owned browser page already open: `list_browser_targets`.
- Browser action the agent must perform (click, type, navigate):
  `capture_browser_scenario` with declared actions. See
  [runtime observation](references/runtime-observation.md) for connect/launch
  and the focused follow-up browser tools.
- Fiddler Everywhere traffic or a native `.saz` capture: read the
  [Fiddler workflow](references/runtime-observation.md#fiddler-everywhere-traffic-debugging).
  Inspect saved SAZ with `inspect_web_network_capture` and `format: "saz"`;
  connect Everywhere's separate MCP server for live traffic.
- Retained HAR/SAZ/native mitmproxy/aioquic qlog capture: `inspect_web_network_capture`. Select
  original record ordinals when useful; inspect producer fields and byte/number
  sidecars without fetching recorded URLs or claiming live attribution. See
  [historical captures](https://github.com/morluto/rea/blob/main/docs/web-network-captures.md) for the exact upstream
  profile and credential exclusions. Qlog support starts with aioquic 1.5.0
  JSON 0.3; stream coverage and endpoint loss declarations do not recover bodies
  or establish network loss. Prefer detail summary, then kind qlog trace/stream
  pages; select one trace, stream ID and direction for contribution/range pages.
  Facts retain all-recorded-events-before-selection scope. Other qlog layouts
  and PCAP correlation are unsupported.
- User-owned Electron runtime already open: `list_electron_targets`. Before an electron-main Inspector attempt, check packaged fuses with `inspect_electron_fuses`; disabled `EnableNodeCliInspectArguments` means the app ignores `--inspect`.
- Packet-field discovery: `inspect_packet_fields` searches installed protocols
  and field names/types before choosing fields for `inspect_packet_capture`.
  Query/page the relevant records; registrations do not establish observed traffic.
- Recorded packet captures: `inspect_packet_capture` with selected TShark fields,
  display filters and decode-as rules. Requires Linux, util-linux prlimit and `REA_TSHARK_COMMAND`; see
  [capture guide](https://github.com/morluto/rea/blob/main/docs/packet-captures.md).
  Packet limits count input packets before filtering. Output defaults to 50 matching
  frames; use `match_offset` / `match_limit` for later pages, or explicit null
  limit for complete matching output. Preserve the source digest across pages.
  This does not perform live capture.
  For address/DNS/SNI/protocol summaries use `inspect_pcap_capture` with MCP
  detail summary, then retained kind pcap pages. Requires Wireshark 4.x tshark
  and capinfos, with Linux prlimit or Windows Job Objects; see
  [packet summaries](https://github.com/morluto/rea/blob/main/docs/pcap-analysis.md).
  Select an exact DNS question for address pages; page exhaustion does not prove
  network completeness. This reads recordings and does not acquire traffic.
- Decoder discovery: `inspect_signal_decoders` searches installed decoder IDs
  or selected decoder help, including channels and options. Query and page the
  relevant details before choosing settings; this does not scan hardware.
- Recorded logic/signal traces: `decode_signal_recording` with explicit decoder,
  channel and protocol settings. On Linux with util-linux prlimit, supply sigrok-cli 0.7.2 through
  `REA_SIGROK_COMMAND`; see [recording guide](https://github.com/morluto/rea/blob/main/docs/signal-recordings.md).
  Output defaults to 50 literal lines; select annotation classes and page with
  `line_offset` / `line_limit`, or explicit null for all remaining output.
  Window counts are display lines, not annotations or samples. Preserve source digests across pages.
  This reads existing files; it does not acquire hardware signals.
- Explicit local WebAssembly artifact: `inspect_wasm_artifact`. Supply WABT 1.0.42
  through `REA_WABT_BIN_DIRECTORY`; retain exact byte/tool identity and decoded WAT.
  Select JavaScript glue and candidate paths explicitly and preserve URL/path
  ambiguity. No implicit fetch or target execution; WAT is not original source.
  See the [WASM guide](https://github.com/morluto/rea/blob/main/docs/wasm-artifacts.md).
- Explicit local EVM bytecode carrier: `inspect_evm_interface` with caller-selected
  `raw` or `hex` encoding. Preserve carrier/decoded digests and treat selectors,
  argument strings and mutability as inferred candidates; this performs no chain
  lookup or target execution. For the complete inferred interface without hex or
  duplicate stdout, discover support and select `detail: "summary"`; complete
  Evidence stays retained under its original identity. Use the returned
  `parent_evidence_id` for exact function or `bytecode_hex`/stdout/stderr pages.
  Candidate coverage does not establish interface completeness. See the
  [EVM bytecode guide](https://github.com/morluto/rea/blob/main/docs/evm-bytecode.md).
- Embedded Go compiler, module or build-setting metadata: `inspect_go_binary`
  with the explicit local file. This built-in target-free inspection requires no
  Go installation or disassembler. Preserve raw module bytes and source ranges;
  absent metadata does not prove a binary is not Go, and unparsed text records
  remain explicit. See the
  [Go binary guide](https://github.com/morluto/rea/blob/main/docs/go-binaries.md).
- Embedded cargo-auditable Rust dependency metadata: `inspect_rust_binary`
  with the explicit local ELF, PE, or thin Mach-O file. This built-in
  target-free inspection requires no Rust installation or disassembler. Preserve
  package order, dependency indices, and the section file range. A missing
  `.dep-v0` section is null metadata, not proof the binary has no dependencies.
  A rustc commit hash is an inference from a read-only `/rustc/<40-hex>/` path.
  See the
  [Rust binary guide](https://github.com/morluto/rea/blob/main/docs/rust-binaries.md).

- Explicit local SQLite database snapshot: `inspect_sqlite_database`. Inspect
  with Node.js 24.x >=24.15 or 26+ providing native SQLite limits. Read schema

# REA

Use REA when a claim depends on a shipped binary or package, decompilation,
passive application runtime evidence, or comparison with
behavior not established by available source. For ordinary analysis of a
complete source repository, use normal repository tools and do not run REA
readiness or provider commands.

## Connect only when needed

Installing this skill supplies instructions; it does not register the REA MCP
server, install analysis engines, or add tools to an already-running agent.

If REA tools are available and their registration is not known to be stale,
proceed directly to the target. Do not run diagnostics or setup before every
investigation. Use the connected server's actual tool list and input schemas;
a skill installed from repository main may describe capabilities absent from
an older npm release. Keep complete inline Evidence when that server does not
advertise retained references.

If tools are absent, a call is blocked by the client, or a required provider is
unavailable, read [connection and recovery](references/connection-and-recovery.md).
Diagnose the observed blocker, continue useful supported work, and resume the
original task after repair. Client approval, shell PATH, registration and engine
availability have different remedies; avoid repeating setup for all of them.

1. Diagnose without changing REA or client configuration. `npx` may download
   the package and write to npm's cache. For Codex, run
   `npx -y rea-agents@6.5.0 doctor --client codex --json`. Substitute the current
   supported client: `claude_code`, `claude_desktop`, `codex`, `cursor`,
   `gemini_cli`, `windsurf`, `devin`, `opencode`, `antigravity`, `copilot_cli`,
   `commandcode`, `vscode`, `grok_build`, `omp`, or `grok_bot`. `grok_bot` has no local
   file registration: doctor reports the Grok Bot chat step, and setup does not
   write `mcp.json`. If the client is unknown, use `doctor --json` and
   inspect its registration results before choosing a setup scope.
2. Distinguish the reason. Missing, malformed, or stale registration needs a
   scoped configuration repair. An aligned registration with no tools in the
   active session needs a restart/reconnection; doctor cannot prove that the
   current agent has connected. A missing provider affects only tasks requiring
   that provider: static JavaScript inspection needs neither Hopper nor Ghidra,
   and Android inspection has separate bring-your-own JADX/Java prerequisites.
3. For a configuration repair, prepare the read-only plan:
   `npx -y rea-agents@6.5.0 setup --client codex --dry-run --json`.
   Use the current client's ID, show its exact proposed paths, backups, and
   changes, and obtain approval before setup writes configuration or installs
   Hopper. Setup normally installs the matching bundled skill too; include that
   replacement in the reviewed plan. After approval, apply the same scope with
   `npx -y rea-agents@6.5.0 setup --client codex --yes`. Add `--install-hopper`
   only if that separate installation was needed and explicitly approved.
4. Restart/reconnect the affected agent. Verify that REA tools actually appear
   in the session, then resume the original investigation. If they remain
   absent, inspect the client's MCP launch error rather than repeating setup.

JADX, Binwalk, or Unblob. Use existing prerequisites; do not install unrelated
software to repair
MCP registration. For an unsupported client, use manual stdio registration
with a version-pinned `rea-agents` package or continue through the CLI.

A concrete CLI fallback for an operator-supplied JavaScript tree or ASAR is:

```bash

```

graph, limitations, and unknowns with the same care as an MCP result; the CLI
returns the Evidence record directly. This fallback does not establish that
MCP is configured. Native CLI tasks still require their selected engine.

is within the authorized scope, use `npx -y rea-agents@6.5.0` in its place.
Configuration repair starts with a read-only setup plan; show paths, backups and
skill replacement before applying authorized changes. Preserve existing approval
and target-execution boundaries. REA setup never installs or upgrades unrelated
software, including Node.js, npm, Homebrew, Java, Ghidra, IDA, JADX, Binwalk or Unblob.

2316:   read-only verify frontier. The exact subset follows the disjoint work

# Shokunin Expertise Axes

What makes a shokunin an expert is decomposed into measurable axes. Every
shokunin works its own subset; the protocol and aggregator lanes own the
fleet-level axes.

## The six axes

| Axis | Definition | Signal an expert shows |
|---|---|---|
| **depth** | Verifiable technical detail — decision tables with real thresholds, named error signatures, cited sources | A reader can act on SKILL.md alone; no filler |
| **coverage** | Fraction of the domain's real surfaces the skill governs (repo paths, tools, edge classes) | PROVINCE.md lists every surface; none unexplored without reason |
| **operability** | Runnable artifacts: checklists that are executable, commands that exist, scripts that run | A checklist item can be run and produces the stated outcome |
| **freshness** | Drift detection — skill claims re-verified against live surfaces; stale items flagged or fixed | Each round LOG entry includes a re-verification result |
| **calibration** | Self-assessment quality: gaps named honestly, confidence graded, overreach caught | SHONEN.md/SCORECARD entries match observed repo state |
| **adjacency** | Cross-domain awareness — evidence belonging to another domain reported, not absorbed | Lane reports name contested scope; integrator arbitrates |

## The learning path

The axes are the unit of work; the learning signal is `LEARNING.md`'s three
trends. Expansion ↔ `coverage` + `adjacency`; quality ↔ `depth` + `freshness`
+ `operability`; discernment ↔ `calibration`. Pick the round's axis from the
trend furthest behind.

## Working an axis

A lane's round is one axis-move: pick the lowest-scoring axis for the repo,
land one verifiable improvement, measure it (file exists / command runs /
citation resolves), record before→after in `SCORECARD.md`, log evidence in
`LOG.md`. If an axis saturates, the lane may retire it or split it into a
sub-axis — recorded in `SCORECARD.md` with reason.

## SCORECARD.md contract (per child repo)

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| axes | Axis name → score 0–10 → evidence pointer → last-change round |
| planned | The single next axis-move the lane intends |
| retired | Axes retired with justification (saturation or wrong fit) |

# Shokunin Corpus Contract

Every shokunin repo carries a proprietary corpus — knowledge about its domain
*and* training lessons about itself. It is the shokunin's memory; it must never
contain generic filler.

## Layout (per child repo)

```
corpus/
  README.md        — index: what's here, coverage map, known gaps, frontier
  QUALITY.md       — the shokunin's own quality bar (LEARNING.md)
  knowledge/       — domain facts, sourced notes, decision records
  lessons/         — training lessons: what worked/failed this round and why
```

Each `knowledge/` entry opens with `source:`, `verified-at:` and `recheck:`;
each `lessons/round-<N>.md` carries a `## Gate` section (candidates,
admitted, rejected with reasons, spot-check result). See `LEARNING.md`.

## Rules

- `knowledge/` entries cite a source: file path, command output, or URL.
- `lessons/` entries cite the round and the evidence (LOG.md round, commit, report).
- A corpus entry is falsifiable or marked opinion; no unverifiable claims.
- The aggregator reviews every corpus each round and files gaps as lessons.

## Rules added from the round-1/2 corpus audits

Evidence: the per-repo `corpus/lessons/round-1-aggregator-audit.md` entries and
`.ufo/reports/round-2/AGGREGATE.md`.

- **A count carries its command.** Any number in a corpus entry (rows, files,
  lines, packages) is written as `<number> — <command> <date>`. Round-1 found
  four unreproducible counts: "275 claim packages" (observed 274 program dirs /
  295 package dirs / 281 `status.json`), "20-row registry" (observed 21),
  "~40 clones" (observed 50), "scripts/ 74 entries" (observed 82).
- **A negative claim carries its sweep.** "No counterexample", "nothing
  handles X", "absent everywhere" need the search command that produced the
  absence, or the claim is unverifiable.
- **A quote names its location.** Frontmatter vs body, header comment vs code,
  script vs installed skill. Round-1 defects: an anti-trigger quoted as
  frontmatter that lives in a body table; a `128`-lane cap attributed to an
  installed skill that contains no `128`.
- **An index row is a claim.** Write the row when the file exists, not before.
  A seeded index naming seven entries while one existed is worse than a
  one-row index.
- **No credential material, ever.** Secret values, session tokens, cookies, and
  vault ref paths (`op://…`) stay out of every corpus, including this one's
  examples. Cite the file path, the mode, and the mechanism; a reader with
  authority can regenerate the metadata.
- **Corrections are new entries, never rewrites.** Lanes own
  `lessons/round-<N>.md`; the aggregator writes only
  `lessons/round-<N>-aggregator-*.md` and does not edit lane-authored corpus
  files in place (same append-only discipline `PROTOCOL.md` gives `LOG.md`).
  This rule exists because of a real collision: aggregator and kagi lane both
  wrote `kagi-shokunin/corpus/lessons/round-1.md` in the same minute
  (2026-09-28 15:56); the lane's committed version was restored and the
  aggregator's moved to `round-1-aggregator-seed.md`.
- **Each round's review emits a verdict per repo** — `conformant` or
  `not conformant`, naming the failed rule and the command that shows it.

[~/Projects/kimi-shokunin/skills/shokunin/protocol/LEARNING.md#5FC7]
1:# Shokunin Learning Path — 修業 (shugyō)
2:
3:A shokunin learns when, across rounds, its corpus **expands**, the **quality**
4:of what it holds rises, and it **recognizes quality** increasingly well. No
5:fixed exam measures this: the domain is not rigidly defined, it keeps
6:growing, and so does the shokunin. Learning is a continual path, walked every
7:round:
8:
9:1. **Curation** — gather candidate material from the domain's real surfaces
10:   (sources, tools, artifacts, practitioners' records, the lane's own work).
11:   Every candidate is judged before it is admitted.
12:2. **Quality gating** — admit into `corpus/knowledge/` only what clears the
13:   shokunin's own bar in `corpus/QUALITY.md`. Every rejection is logged with
14:   its reason; a rejection is evidence of taste, not wasted work.

displayContent.text:
# Shokunin Learning Path — 修業 (shugyō)

A shokunin learns when, across rounds, its corpus **expands**, the **quality**
of what it holds rises, and it **recognizes quality** increasingly well. No
fixed exam measures this: the domain is not rigidly defined, it keeps
growing, and so does the shokunin. Learning is a continual path, walked every
round:

1. **Curation** — gather candidate material from the domain's real surfaces
   (sources, tools, artifacts, practitioners' records, the lane's own work).
   Every candidate is judged before it is admitted.
2. **Quality gating** — admit into `corpus/knowledge/` only what clears the
   shokunin's own bar in `corpus/QUALITY.md`. Every rejection is logged with
   its reason; a rejection is evidence of taste, not wasted work.
3. **Understanding** — distill what was admitted: connect entries, state the
   principle behind them, fold durable understanding into `SKILL.md`
   (decision tables, error patterns, checklists), and sharpen `QUALITY.md`
   from what the gate got right and wrong.
4. **Expanding perspective** — work the province frontier: adjacent
   sub-areas, other tools, schools and viewpoints, counter-examples and
   failure cases. The province grows by evidence, not by declaration.

## The three trends — one verdict each, every round

Verdicts use the protocol vocabulary (`improved`, `harmed`, `unchanged`,
`unprovable-but-better`); no trend is a scalar.

| Trend | Observable | `improved` when | `harmed` when |
|---|---|---|---|
| **expansion** | admitted `knowledge/` entries on ground the coverage map did not hold; frontier areas entered; new kinds of source | net new admitted entries on uncovered ground, each citing its coverage-map row | an admitted entry fails the bar it was admitted under |
| **quality** | entries re-verified, deepened, or superseded by stronger ones; `verified-at` freshness | a weaker entry is superseded by a stronger one, or stale entries re-verify, with no admitted entry failing its re-check | an entry is found false or stale and left unmarked |
| **discernment** | gate decisions vs the outside spot-check; `QUALITY.md` criteria | the spot-check agrees with the gate on admits *and* rejects, or a disagreement becomes a lesson that adds a grounded `QUALITY.md` criterion | a disagreement is left unlearned, or a criterion is added with no lesson behind it |

Growth without quality is not learning: `expansion: improved` with
`quality: harmed` is a trade, reported as a trade, never admitted.

## Discernment is checked from outside

Self-assessed taste is not discernment. Each round a non-author — a fresh
reviewer or the operator — spot-checks a sample of that round's gate
decisions, **at least one admit and one reject**, and records
`agree`/`disagree` with a reason in the round's lesson. A subagent the lane
dispatched is still the lane.

Operator teaching outranks every other source. A teaching lands verbatim as
`corpus/lessons/operator-<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md`; by the lane's next round it
must be reflected in `QUALITY.md` or `SKILL.md`, with the lesson cited, or the
round reports why not.

## Files the path writes

- `corpus/QUALITY.md` — the shokunin's quality bar for its own domain: what
  makes a source or entry strong, the signals of weak material, admission
  criteria. Thin at mint; every criterion cites the lesson that produced it.
  Criteria are superseded by new rows that name the row they replace, never
  rewritten.
- `corpus/README.md` — the coverage map plus a `## Frontier` list of areas
  being explored and not yet held.
- `corpus/knowledge/<slug>.md` — opens with `source:`, `verified-at:` (commit
  or date) and `recheck:` (the command or citation that re-verifies it).
- `corpus/lessons/round-<N>.md` — carries a `## Gate` section: candidates
  considered, admitted, rejected (with reasons), and the spot-check result.

## Province is a frontier, not a fence

`PROVINCE.md` holds **Core** (surfaces owned now), **Frontier** (areas being
explored; expected to grow) and **Adjacent** (sibling-owned; report, don't
absorb). Moving frontier ground into core is ordinary growth, recorded in
`LOG.md`. The one-domain-per-shokunin invariant still holds where a sibling
already owns the ground: contested scope is reported, never silently
absorbed.

## Relation to the axes

The trends are the learning signal; `AXES.md` axis-moves remain the unit of
work. Expansion is served by `coverage` and `adjacency`; quality by `depth`,
`freshness` and `operability`; discernment by `calibration`. Choose a round's
one axis-move from the trend that is furthest behind.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Resolve the tracked script target, not the link directory — the sibling
# wrapper anchor (self-iter.sh/dev-verify.sh/smoke.sh): BASH_SOURCE[0]
# carries the caller's path (a bare PATH lookup or an external symlink), so
# readlink -f anchors ROOT to the real scripts/ directory. An empty source
# (stdin invocation) or an unresolvable one fails typed here instead of
# silently exec'ing a nonexistent ufo-sighting.mjs from the link tree.
SCRIPT_SOURCE="${BASH_SOURCE[0]:-}"
SCRIPT_PATH=""
if [[ -n "$SCRIPT_SOURCE" ]]; then
  SCRIPT_PATH="$(readlink -f -- "$SCRIPT_SOURCE" 2>/dev/null)" || SCRIPT_PATH=""
fi
[[ -n "$SCRIPT_PATH" && -f "$SCRIPT_PATH" ]] || {
  echo "cannot resolve scripts/ufo-sighting source: ${SCRIPT_SOURCE:-<none>} — invoke it by path (e.g. bash scripts/ufo-sighting)" >&2
  exit 2
}
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$SCRIPT_PATH")/.." && pwd)"

# Node's compile cache only covers the entry module when it is set via the
# environment (module.enableCompileCache() runs too late for the file being
# executed). ~2-4ms off every status poll; an operator-set value wins.
export NODE_COMPILE_CACHE="${NODE_COMPILE_CACHE:-$ROOT/.ufo/cache/node-compile}"

if [[ "${UFO_SIGHTING_ATTACH:-}" == "1" && $# -eq 0 ]]; then
  TMUX_ARGS=()
  if [[ -n "${UFO_SIGHTING_TMUX_SOCKET:-}" ]]; then
    # Same gate as tmuxPrefix() in ufo-sighting.mjs: the socket name reaches
    # tmux -L verbatim, so reject anything outside the declared grammar here
    # too instead of letting tmux fail untyped.
    [[ "$UFO_SIGHTING_TMUX_SOCKET" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,80}$ ]] || { echo "invalid tmux socket override" >&2; exit 2; }
    TMUX_ARGS=(-L "$UFO_SIGHTING_TMUX_SOCKET")
  fi
  exec tmux "${TMUX_ARGS[@]}" attach-session -d -t 'ufo_sighting:1'
fi

if [[ "${1:-}" == "--ufo-sighting-inquiry-direct" ]]; then
  [[ $# -eq 4 ]] || { echo "invalid internal inquiry invocation" >&2; exit 2; }
  SESSION_DIR="$2"
  SLUG="$3"
  PROMPT_FILE="$4"
  # The prompt reaches omp as a @file message argument (content inlined by
  # omp), never inline argv — a >128KiB prompt cannot hit E2BIG, and NULs or
  # trailing newlines survive verbatim (command substitution would strip
  # both). Keep the 1 MiB bound (parity with MAX_INQUIRY_PROMPT_BYTES in
  # ufo-sighting.mjs): read with a hard byte cap instead of stat-then-read so
  # a growing file cannot race past the bound, and count BYTES not chars —
  # ${#var} counts characters and would undercount multi-byte UTF-8.
  # Single read: two separate head calls would let a growing file race the
  # bound (first read small, second read large). Capture once, count once.
  # Snapshot the prompt into the session dir: the byte check and the omp
  # @file read are separate opens, so a replaced/growing file could race
  # past the bound or swap content between check and exec. Copy once into a
  # private file inside SESSION_DIR (per-invocation state, cleaned with the
  # session — exec never runs an EXIT trap, so TMPDIR would leak it).
  SNAP="$SESSION_DIR/.inquiry-prompt.snapshot"
  head -c 1048577 -- "$PROMPT_FILE" > "$SNAP" 2>/dev/null || { echo "cannot read inquiry prompt" >&2; exit 2; }
  chmod 600 "$SNAP" 2>/dev/null || true
  PROMPT_HEAD="$(wc -c < "$SNAP")" || { echo "cannot read inquiry prompt" >&2; exit 2; }
  [[ "$PROMPT_HEAD" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$PROMPT_HEAD" -le 1048576 ]] || { echo "inquiry prompt exceeds 1048576 bytes" >&2; exit 2; }
  # Strip control chars from the slug before it reaches the OSC title escape.
  SLUG="${SLUG//[[:cntrl:]]/}"
  printf '\033]0;ufo-sighting: %s\007' "$SLUG"
  exec omp --cwd "$ROOT" --session-dir "$SESSION_DIR" --no-title --max-time 30m --model @slow "@$SNAP"
fi

if [[ "${1:-}" == "--ufo-sighting-native-direct" ]]; then
  shift
  exec node "$ROOT/scripts/run-omp-native-trial.mjs" --interactive "$@"
fi

if [[ "${1:-}" == "--inquiry" ]]; then
  [[ $# -eq 2 ]] || { echo "usage: ufo-sighting --inquiry PROMPT_FILE" >&2; exit 2; }
  PROMPT_FILE="$(realpath -- "$2" 2>/dev/null)" || { echo "cannot resolve inquiry prompt: $2" >&2; exit 2; }
  [[ -f "$PROMPT_FILE" ]] || { echo "missing inquiry prompt: $PROMPT_FILE" >&2; exit 2; }
  SLUG="${PROMPT_FILE##*/}"
  SLUG="${SLUG%%.*}"
  SLUG="${SLUG//[[:cntrl:]]/}"
  if [[ -n "${UFO_SIGHTING_SESSION_DIR:-}" ]]; then
    SESSION_DIR="$UFO_SIGHTING_SESSION_DIR"
  else
    # tmp writes persist to the second-NVMe scratch root when present.
    TMPBASE="${TMPDIR:-}"
    [[ -d "$TMPBASE" ]] || TMPBASE="/scratch/tmp"
    [[ -d "$TMPBASE" ]] || TMPBASE="/tmp"
    SESSION_DIR="$(mktemp -d "${TMPBASE}/ufo-sighting-${SLUG}-XXXXXX")" || { echo "cannot create session dir" >&2; exit 2; }
  fi
  exec node "$ROOT/scripts/ufo-sighting.mjs" inquiry \
    --prompt "$PROMPT_FILE" \
    --slug "$SLUG" \
    --session-dir "$SESSION_DIR"
fi

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Validate this round's pinned evidence package, not semantic truth or admission."""
import argparse
import copy
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = HERE.parents[2]
RESULT = Path("evidence/round-1-2026-10-15/result.json")


class Finding(Exception):
    def __init__(self, code, name):
        self.code, self.name = code, name


def require(condition, name, code=1):
    if not condition:
        raise Finding(code, name)


def load(path):
    return json.loads(path.read_text())


def check(root, expected, admission=False):
    for path, digest in expected["snapshots"].items():
        file = root / path
        require(file.is_file(), "snapshot_missing", 2)
        require(hashlib.sha256(file.read_bytes()).hexdigest() == digest,
                "snapshot_tampered", 2)
    require((root / RESULT).is_file(), "missing_result", 2)
    result = load(root / RESULT)
    require(result["baseline_revision"] == expected["baseline_revision"]
            and result["measured_revision"] == expected["measured_revision"],
            "revision_mismatch")
    obligations = result["obligations"]
    ids = [row["id"] for row in obligations]
    require(sorted(ids) == expected["obligation_ids"], "obligation_set_mismatch")
    require(all(row["status"] == "aligned" and row["reviewer"] == "L1-author"
                and row["source_review"] for row in obligations), "review_incomplete")
    require(result["admitted"] is False and result["verified_round_increment"] == 0
            and result["outside_spot_check"] is False, "unearned_admission")
    require(result["smoke"]["subject_sha256"] == expected["smoke"]["subject_sha256"],
            "subject_mismatch")
    bundle = load(root / expected["bundle_path"])
    records = [r for r in bundle["records"]
               if r["evidence_id"] == expected["smoke"]["evidence_id"]]
    require(len(records) == 1, "smoke_record_mismatch")
    record = records[0]
    require(record["subject"]["digest"]["sha256"] == result["smoke"]["subject_sha256"]
            and record["subject"]["local_path"] == expected["smoke"]["path"],
            "subject_mismatch")
    require(record["operation"] == "inspect_native_instruction"
            and record["parameters"]["address"] == "0x117070"
            and record["confidence"] == "observed"
            and record["authority"] == "shipped-artifact", "smoke_authority_mismatch")
    instruction = record["normalized_result"]
    require(instruction["status"] == "decoded" and instruction["bytes"] == "f30f1efa"
            and instruction["length"] == 4 and instruction["mnemonic"] == "ENDBR64",
            "smoke_instruction_mismatch")
    measurements = load(root / expected["measurements_path"])
    for stage in ("baseline", "after"):
        require(measurements[stage] == expected["controls"][stage], "control_mismatch")
    wave = load(root / expected["wave_validation_path"])
    require(wave["exit_code"] == 0 and wave["dispatched"] is False,
            "wave_state_mismatch")
    plan = json.loads(wave["stdout"])
    require(plan["counts"] == {"spawn": 32, "resume": 0, "total": 32},
            "wave_count_mismatch")
    require(len({t["name"] for t in plan["tasks"]}) == 32,
            "wave_count_mismatch")
    if admission:
        # This recovery has no dispatched wave or applicable task-receipt binding.
        # A later sound round needs new evidence, never a flipped acceptance flag.
        raise Finding(2, "required_alias_bindings_missing+applicable_receipt_binding_missing")
    return "RECOVERY_EVIDENCE: CLEAN finding=pinned_package_consistent author_review=9/9 coverage=70/72 citation_rules=9/9 admitted=false verified_round_increment=0"


def selftest(expected):
    result = load(ROOT / RESULT)
    cases = expected["selftest"]
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="gate-selftest-", dir=HERE) as directory:
        fixture = Path(directory)
        for relative in expected["snapshots"]:
            target = fixture / relative
            target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            target.write_bytes((ROOT / relative).read_bytes())
        target = fixture / RESULT
        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        for case in cases:
            candidate = copy.deepcopy(result)
            name = case["case"]
            if name == "wrong_revision":
                candidate["measured_revision"] = "0" * 40
            elif name == "omitted_obligation":
                candidate["obligations"].pop()
            elif name == "duplicate_obligation":
                candidate["obligations"][-1] = candidate["obligations"][0]
            elif name == "wrong_subject":
                candidate["smoke"]["subject_sha256"] = "0" * 64
            elif name == "unearned_admission":
                candidate["admitted"] = True
            target.write_text(json.dumps(candidate))
            snapshot = fixture / expected["bundle_path"]
            original = snapshot.read_bytes()
            if name == "snapshot_tampered":
                snapshot.write_bytes(original + b" ")
            if name == "missing_result":
                target.unlink()
            command = [sys.executable, str(Path(__file__).resolve()), "--root", str(fixture)]
            if name == "blocked_admission":
                command.append("--admission")
            run = subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True, text=True)
            snapshot.write_bytes(original)
            passed = run.returncode == case["exit_code"] and case["finding"] in run.stdout
            print(f"SELFTEST_CASE: {'CLEAN' if passed else 'FAILED'} case={name} exit={run.returncode} expected={case['exit_code']} finding={case['finding']}")
            require(passed, "selftest_case_failed")
    return f"RECOVERY_SELFTEST: CLEAN cases={len(cases)} exit=0"


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--root", type=Path, default=ROOT)
    parser.add_argument("--admission", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--selftest", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    label = "ROUND_ADMISSION" if args.admission else "RECOVERY_EVIDENCE"
    try:
        expected = load(HERE / "expected.json")
        print(selftest(expected) if args.selftest else check(args.root, expected, args.admission))
        return 0
    except Finding as error:
        state = "COULD_NOT_EVALUATE" if error.code == 2 else "FAILED"
        print(f"{label}: {state} finding={error.name} exit={error.code}")
        return error.code
    except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError, TypeError):
        print(f"{label}: COULD_NOT_EVALUATE finding=unreadable_or_invalid_input exit=2")
        return 2


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

    require(len(records) == 1, "smoke_record_mismatch")
    record = records[0]
    require(record["subject"]["digest"]["sha256"] == result["smoke"]["subject_sha256"]
            and record["subject"]["local_path"] == expected["smoke"]["path"],
            "subject_mismatch")
    require(record["operation"] == "inspect_native_instruction"
            and record["parameters"]["address"] == "0x117070"
            and record["confidence"] == "observed"
            and record["authority"] == "shipped-artifact", "smoke_authority_mismatch")
    instruction = record["normalized_result"]
    require(instruction["status"] == "decoded" and instruction["bytes"] == "f30f1efa"
            and instruction["length"] == 4 and instruction["mnemonic"] == "ENDBR64",
            "smoke_instruction_mismatch")
    measurements = load(root / expected["measurements_path"])
    for stage in ("baseline", "after"):
        require(measurements[stage] == expected["controls"][stage], "control_mismatch")
    wave = load(root / expected["wave_validation_path"])
    require(wave["exit_code"] == 0 and wave["dispatched"] is False,
            "wave_state_mismatch")
    plan = json.loads(wave["stdout"])
    require(plan["counts"] == {"spawn": 32, "resume": 0, "total": 32},
            "wave_count_mismatch")
    require(len({t["name"] for t in plan["tasks"]}) == 32,
            "wave_count_mismatch")
    if admission:
        # This recovery has no dispatched wave or applicable task-receipt binding.
        # A later sound round needs new evidence, never a flipped acceptance flag.
        raise Finding(2, "required_alias_bindings_missing+applicable_receipt_binding_missing")
    return "RECOVERY_EVIDENCE: CLEAN finding=pinned_package_consistent author_review=9/9 coverage=70/72 citation_rules=9/9 admitted=false verified_round_increment=0"


def selftest(expected):
    result = load(ROOT / RESULT)
    cases = expected["selftest"]
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="gate-selftest-", dir=HERE) as directory:
        fixture = Path(directory)
        for relative in expected["snapshots"]:
            target = fixture / relative
            target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            target.write_bytes((ROOT / relative).read_bytes())
        target = fixture / RESULT
        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        for case in cases:
            candidate = copy.deepcopy(result)
            name = case["case"]
            if name == "wrong_revision":
                candidate["measured_revision"] = "0" * 40
            elif name == "omitted_obligation":
                candidate["obligations"].pop()
            elif name == "duplicate_obligation":
                candidate["obligations"][-1] = candidate["obligations"][0]
            elif name == "wrong_subject":
                candidate["smoke"]["subject_sha256"] = "0" * 64
            elif name == "unearned_admission":
                candidate["admitted"] = True
            target.write_text(json.dumps(candidate))
            snapshot = fixture / expected["bundle_path"]
            original = snapshot.read_bytes()
            if name == "snapshot_tampered":
                snapshot.write_bytes(original + b" ")
            if name == "missing_result":
                target.unlink()
            command = [sys.executable, str(Path(__file__).resolve()), "--root", str(fixture)]
            if name == "blocked_admission":
                command.append("--admission")
            run = subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True, text=True)
            snapshot.write_bytes(original)
            passed = run.returncode == case["exit_code"] and case["finding"] in run.stdout
            print(f"SELFTEST_CASE: {'CLEAN' if passed else 'FAILED'} case={name} exit={run.returncode} expected={case['exit_code']} finding={case['finding']}")
            require(passed, "selftest_case_failed")
    return f"RECOVERY_SELFTEST: CLEAN cases={len(cases)} exit=0"


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--root", type=Path, default=ROOT)
    parser.add_argument("--admission", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--selftest", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    label = "ROUND_ADMISSION" if args.admission else "RECOVERY_EVIDENCE"
    try:
        expected = load(HERE / "expected.json")
        print(selftest(expected) if args.selftest else check(args.root, expected, args.admission))
        return 0
    except Finding as error:
        state = "COULD_NOT_EVALUATE" if error.code == 2 else "FAILED"
        print(f"{label}: {state} finding={error.name} exit={error.code}")
        return error.code
    except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError, TypeError):
        print(f"{label}: COULD_NOT_EVALUATE finding=unreadable_or_invalid_input exit=2")
        return 2


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
"}

# 2026-10-15 — round 1 recovery: a landed assessment is not a verified round

source: `LOG.md`, Interactive round-1 recovery; `c265db9bd3c0883fbaf4487f839559c85a736826`; `.ufo/rounds/interactive-r1/`
verified-at: 2026-10-15; recovery evidence only, round admission blocked
recheck: `python3 .ufo/rounds/interactive-r1/verify-recovery.py`; `--selftest`; `--admission`; source-count recipes A/B in SCORECARD

## Trigger and correction

The interrupted worker landed the calibration assessment at `c265db9`, but
its scorecard, lesson and log cited an absent `result.json`. The interactive
successor found the inherited rubric, baseline and native bundle, no local
round report, and only untracked native-session material. Preserve those
artifacts and the historical r1–14 labels; do not infer a completed round from
the old launch counter or commit subject. This is recovery of the existing
2026-10-15 round 1, not another round and not the next version-expansion move.

This entry supersedes the closure promises in
`corpus/lessons/2026-10-15-round-1.md:140-143,154-160` and `LOG.md:480-484`:
the local result is now restored, but no fleet report reassessment was written
and no specialist/outside-review attribution was reconstructed from transcripts.
Only this repository is writable. The new result's C1–C9 reviews are explicitly
**L1-author** reviews, not proof that the interrupted worker finished those reviews.

## Fresh observations

- Immutable Git-object measurement for baseline `6645585873c4e66372b15687c47000abf8d91978`
  and work commit `c265db9bd3c0883fbaf4487f839559c85a736826` reproduced **70/72**
  map coverage and **9/9** resolvable rule blocks at both revisions. Counting
  recipe A is in SCORECARD; fresh outputs are
  `.ufo/rounds/interactive-r1/source-measurements.json`. These remain structural
  proxies, not coverage of the whole domain or semantic correctness.
- Counting recipe B, executed with `/usr/bin/jq --slurpfile r
  evidence/round-1-2026-10-15/result.json ...
  evidence/round-1-2026-10-15/rubric.json`, returned baseline **0/9, score 0**
  and after **9/9, score 10**, measured against those two source commits.
  The result records each source-review argument; counting flags does not
  prove their truth. Failure-selected completeness is not unbiased accuracy.
- The current live REA status reported a closed target, package **6.5.0**,
  **207** MCP tools, **153** CLI commands, skill **42**, catalog digest
  `805433f17bb4f709558ff20c04f96fe561fca2938fd0f459b1f8cc0f6b438ded`.
  These are catalog/status facts, not 207 held verbs. No host config,
  package or provider remediation was performed.
- Actual smoke: pin `/usr/lib/libjq.so.1.0.4` at SHA-256
  `7e8bccc6df37a55fb90703c9069b3770f5cdc502e96959c866d2f30fbf5e8b6b`;
  `open_binary` with Ghidra; `inspect_native_instruction {"address":"0x117070"}`
  decoded `f30f1efa` / `ENDBR64`, length 4, observed/shipped-artifact, provider
  **12.1.4**. Exported the complete fresh bundle to
  `.ufo/rounds/interactive-r1/rea-bundle.json`, then closed only that owned
  session (`result:null`). Evidence
  `ev_f5e5da50ea8ff88ca9b26a97cebe1ac440c41414e0effd9bfe1943f464780481`.
  `sha256sum /usr/lib/libjq.so.1.0.4 && objdump -d --start-address=0x17070
  --stop-address=0x17074 /usr/lib/libjq.so.1.0.4` independently matched digest
  and bytes, exit 0. This is static decoding, not target execution or safety.

## Gate

- **Candidates considered:** restore the missing assessment result and local
  handoff; start the next round immediately; dispatch through whichever aliases
  happen to work; count historical quota or a clean evidence gate as 100-round
  progress; manufacture a receipt from local prompt hashes.
- **Admitted to this recovery lesson:** only source-backed chronology,
  reproducible measurements, a bounded static smoke, and truthful blockers.
  No new `knowledge/` surface is admitted; no complete round is admitted.
- **Rejected:** unauthorized alias substitution, invented worker/outside review,
  numeric mastery, silent renumbering, availability-to-holding inference,
  receipt fabrication and Sighting completion without applicable authority.
- **Local checks:** before the repair, the recovery gate returned
  `COULD_NOT_EVALUATE finding=missing_result`, exit **2**. After the repair,
  `RECOVERY_EVIDENCE: CLEAN ... admitted=false verified_round_increment=0`,
  exit **0**; isolated self-invocation tested **9** exit/finding pairs and
  returned `RECOVERY_SELFTEST: CLEAN cases=9 exit=0`. Full output, commands
  and process exit codes are in `.ufo/rounds/interactive-r1/gate-before.json`
  and `gate-results.json`. The gate pins every input snapshot digest; it
  checks package integrity and cross-references, not review semantics.
- **Admission check:** `--admission` returned
  `ROUND_ADMISSION: COULD_NOT_EVALUATE finding=required_alias_bindings_missing+applicable_receipt_binding_missing exit=2`.
  This negative prerequisite verdict is not canonical native judgment.
- **Spot-check:** no outside admit/reject review occurred. Planned specialists
  were not dispatched; author review is not discernment or promotion evidence.

## Exact blockers and unblock actions

The canonical `ufo-swarm-wave.mjs plan --spec <saved-wave-spec> --route-families`
accepted **32** distinct scopes, width **32**, exit **0**. The full validation
output is saved locally. It did not dispatch or establish route health.

| Binding | Required | Observed in global taxonomy overrides |
|---|---|---|
| executor / scribe | `@m_composer` | `@m_mid` / `@m_fast` |
| reviewer / critic | `@m_grok` | `@m_mid` / `@m_strong` |
| connector | `@m_antigravity`, fallback `@m_zfl` | `@m_mid`; named antigravity chain is empty |

A model-binding sweep of existing global agent cards found no alternate
binding. No wave was dispatched, no new L1 was spawned, and no pins, routing
overlays or global config changes were used. Operator/integrator action:
provide the required existing role bindings and connector fallback before
redispatching the saved scopes through one complete native task batch.

The selected launch and Sighting metadata identifies run/session
`shk-kaidoku-interactive-20261015T050057Z`, mission
`m_645cfa32b5284aaab568431141665df8`, pane `%14`, with an `argv` dispatch.
It supplies no taskKey, dispatcher prompt/config digests or receipt/result
binding. `.ufo/rounds/interactive-r1/receipt-binding-observation.json` records
only metadata shape. Operator/integrator action: issue an applicable
receipt-bound dispatch; local arbitrary hashes cannot substitute for it.
No receipt mint/validation or Sighting completion is claimed.

## Verdict and continuation

For the inherited source move: calibration **improved** within its nine-item
selected rubric; coverage/depth **unchanged**. Recovery itself repairs evidence
durability, not another scored round. Trends: expansion **unchanged**,
quality **improved** only for this assessment evidence chain, discernment
**unchanged**. Retain all named provider, identity-law, map, scope and fleet
history debt. No saturation, promotion or harmed-axis trade is asserted.

**Verified-round increment: 0.** Recover round 1 in a fresh authorized session
when the bindings are supplied; do not advance to round 2 or run an in-session
loop. Historical quotas and the goal of at least 100 verified rounds remain
separate from actual applicable completion evidence.

---
name: kaidoku-shokunin
description: Domain specialist — reverse engineering of shipped artifacts with REA on this Linux host — native ELF/PE through the Ghidra 12.1.4 provider, Electron/ASAR/JavaScript bundles, archives and packages, managed assemblies, firmware images and recorded crashes; evidence-first static analysis that keeps observation, inference and unknowns separate. Trigger on "shipped binary", "decompile", "what does this .asar/.exe/ELF do", "compare two versions of this package", "analyze this core dump". Anti-trigger: ordinary source repositories — use normal repo tools, never run REA on available source. Rank: shonen.
---

# kaidoku-shokunin

## Domain

Reverse engineering of shipped artifacts with REA on this Linux host. Owned
surfaces (verified 2026-10-13, see PROVINCE.md): the `rea` MCP server + CLI
(`npx -y rea-agents@6.4.0`, 170 tools / 127 commands), the Ghidra 12.1.4
provider (`/home/vgpnk/.local/opt/ghidra_12.1.4_PUBLIC`, JDK 21), ELF analysis
end-to-end (`analyze`/`search`/`decompile` verified on `/usr/bin/jq`),
ASAR/JavaScript analysis (`analyze_javascript_application` verified on
`default_app.asar`), archive/package inventory, and host binutils fallbacks.

Drift-sensitive values: `GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR`, `JAVA_HOME` in the three client
configs (devin/omp/kimi), the pinned `rea-agents@6.4.0`, the installed skill
version. Probe convention: `rea doctor` = environment verdict (read
`scope_checks[]`, not the top-level bool), `binary_session {}` = live verdict —
a catalog-listed tool is available, not held.

## Working contract

- Route the target first (decision table below). All verified on this host
  2026-10-13; a catalog-listed tool is available, not held — `held` requires a
  carrier run this round (QUALITY.md #10).
- Work summary-first: `detail:"summary"` → `parent_evidence_id` →
  `inspect_analysis_view`. Never re-run a producer to read one object.
- Label every conclusion observation / inference / unknown. Static output is
  never "observed execution". See `corpus/knowledge/2026-10-13-elf-observation-jq.md`.
- Pin the target: path + sha256 before any analysis; magic bytes are not
  format proof (`0xCAFEBABE` bin → `mach-o-universal` false positive).
- Sessions are ephemeral `/tmp/rea-ghidra-*`, shared across lanes — never
  clean another session's dir. `--snapshot` persists evidence, not the DB.

## Decision table (this host, r3-verified)

| Target | First move | Status |
|---|---|---|
| ELF exe/lib | `rea analyze` → `search` → `decompile`/`function` | held (jq, libjq) |
| `.so`/`.node` vaddr | `nm` addr **+0x100000** = REA addr; confirm via `address-to-file-offset` | held |
| PE x86-64 / ARM64 | `rea analyze` (Ghidra PeLoader, wine-free) | held (cli-64, cli-arm64) |
| `.asar`/JS bundle | `analyze_javascript_application`; >~4MB single files OOM → extract + `--artifact-format directory` | held (obsidian ×2, typora, signal census) |
| Archive/APK | `inspect-artifact` → content graph; `.so` members → extract + `analyze` | held (Godot APK) |
| AppImage | `analyze` (ELF only); payload via `read-bytes unallocated_0:0x…` | held; `extract-artifact` has no ELF reader |
| Recorded core ≤32MiB | `coredumpctl dump` (output already decompressed ELF — no `zstd -d`) → `inspect-recorded-crash` (needs `REA_PWNTOOLS_PYTHON` uv venv) | held; >32MiB cores refused `out_of_range` |
| Mach-O synth carrier | `inspect-keyed-archive`, `decode-interface-builder`, `trace-dylib-resolution` | held on synth carriers (recipes in corpus) |
| EVM bytecode | `inspect-evm-interface <file> <raw|hex>` — encoding POSITIONAL | held (selector recovery) |
| Runtime targets | self-launch `chromium --remote-debugging-port=9222` / `xvfb-run electron …:9223` → `list-*-targets` → `inspect-*-page` | held |
| `.jsc` V8 bytecode | `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1` + version-matched electron (V8 map in corpus) → `--print-bytecode` | held r4 (typora→electron42.2.0) |
| Firmware blob | `inspect-firmware-regions` (binwalk 3.1.0), `extract-firmware` (unblob 26.6.4) | held r4u; RISC-V `target_unavailable` bypassed via e_machine patch + language override (r5-01) |
| Android APK | `inspect-android-package`/`decode-android-resources`/`inspect-android-method` (jadx-mcp 0.7.1, apktool 3.0.3) | held r4u; real Java decompile |
| Managed DLL `0x14c` | `inspect-managed-artifact`/`inspect-managed-members` <64MiB; else dnfile+dncil | held r4/r4u; `0xfd1d` class → dnfile only |
| JS minified source | `recover-javascript-sources <FILE> <outdir>` (file arg; wakaru ELF binding) | held r4u |
| JS runtime verbs | `observe-web-session`/`observe-javascript-runtime`/`reconcile-javascript-runtime` on self-launched targets | held r4; `capture-electron-scenario` refused |
| Binary layout | `inspect-binary-layout` (pwntools venv `~/.local/share/kaidoku-pwnenv`) | held r4 |
| adb (device-free) | `inspect-adb-client`, `list-adb-devices` only — 22/24 need a device | held r4u |
| AppImage inner | unblob carve at `--appimage-offset` → `7z` on squashfs → inner asar analyze | held r4 |
| >90MB PE | `provider_timeout` at ~900s internal deadline — raise `REA_GHIDRA_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS`+`GHIDRA_HEADLESS_MAXMEM` | measured r4 |
| IDA/Hopper/JEB | env keys absent | frontier |

## Error patterns (typed refusals)

| Error | Meaning | Move |
|---|---|---|
| `provider_unavailable`, retryable:true | provider engine absent (`REA_PWNTOOLS_PYTHON`, `REA_IDA_MCP_CONFIG`) | operator-owned env key; retryable after provisioning |
| `capability_unavailable`/`unsupported_provider`, retryable:false | tool absent (`REA_JADX_MCP_JAR`, `REA_APKTOOL_COMMAND`, `REA_BINWALK_COMMAND` 3.1.x, `REA_UNBLOB_COMMAND` 26.6.x, `REA_WAKARU_COMMAND`) | both kinds exit **1** — check `retryable`, not RC |
| `unsupported_target` | wrong carrier (plain plist, >32MiB core, ELF→`extract-artifact`, `binary_overview`→paging) | change carrier, not args |
| `unsupported PE architecture` | managed DLL of refused class (x64 R2R `0xfd1d`, x64 IL-only) — `0x14c` IL-only works | dnfile+dncil covers the refused class |
| `provider_timeout` | internal ~900s session deadline (GhidraClient.js:607), not outer `timeout` | raise env timeouts + heap; measured at 91.6MB PE |
| `Unknown flag` | arg is positional (evm encoding, keyed-archive `archive`, addresses) | schema properties ≠ argv flags |
| `out_of_range` | input exceeds cap (32 MiB crash, 16 MiB EVM file) | split/dump subrange |
| `invalid_format`/`invalid_input` | syntax (e.g. `search` needs `--mode regex --pattern '.*'`; `.zst` not a core) | re-shape input |

## Queue-drain craft (rounds 5-12, distilled in round 13)

Decision rules distilled from the round 5–13 queue-drain corpus entries; each
bullet is bounded by the lines it cites.

- **Evidence ids are content-addressed per verb family — never substitute ids
  across invocation shapes.** Many families re-derive byte-identical ids and
  envelopes across re-runs, lanes, and rounds (native verbs
  `corpus/knowledge/2026-10-13-r7-01-queue-a-ops.md:84-91`; JS workflows
  `corpus/knowledge/2026-10-13-r8-02-queue-a-ops-2.md:99-123`; ledger verb
  `corpus/knowledge/2026-10-14-r9-01-queue-a-ops.md:221-249`; an id held
  across a day and re-derives byte-exact
  `corpus/knowledge/2026-10-14-r12-01-queue-b-ready.md:11`). Per-run id
  classes are recorded too: raw_result embeds a mkdtemp staging path (jadx,
  firmware-regions —

  treat a pass as input correctness; cross-check independently

  recorded instances of rows queued while already held: row 7 / table line

  can be incomplete in BOTH directions
  (`corpus/knowledge/2026-10-14-r11-01-queue-ops.md:72-74`) — and the

  (`corpus/knowledge/2026-10-14-r12-01-queue-b-ready.md:23`).

reproducing call cited? providers `status` (not per-op `available`)? versions
pinned (rea-agents@6.4.0, Ghidra 12.1.4, JDK 21)?

## Known limits (r4)

  `changed` needs ALL bundle members paired.
- MCP session retention is epoch-scoped; `evidence_links` pin records across
  targets; evidence ids are `f(content, path, params)` — deterministic on
  same-path re-runs, NOT path-independent (cite `subject.digest.sha256` for
  cross-path identity).

  working tool can still OOM in REA's spawn context. Bind native ELF binaries
  over node shims (`REA_WAKARU_COMMAND` → `@wakaru/cli-linux-x64/wakaru`).

  (file not dir, output dir must be absent), `inspect-evm-interface <path>
  <encoding>`, `extract-artifact` ignores extra positionals silently.

## Refuses

Malware triage at scale, non-REA dynamic analysis (gdb scripting, strace,
Frida), source-repo reconstruction, all engine/tooling installs, and
safety/quality verdicts on findings (Adjacent — report to orchestrator, never
absorb; PROVINCE.md). Boundary: "what does this shipped artifact do, per
evidence id X" — never "is it safe or trustworthy".

---
name: kaidoku-shokunin
description: Domain specialist — reverse engineering of shipped artifacts with REA on this Linux host — native ELF/PE through the Ghidra 12.1.4 provider, Electron/ASAR/JavaScript bundles, archives and packages, managed assemblies, firmware images and recorded crashes; evidence-first static analysis that keeps observation, inference and unknowns separate. Trigger on "shipped binary", "decompile", "what does this .asar/.exe/ELF do", "compare two versions of this package", "analyze this core dump". Anti-trigger: ordinary source repositories — use normal repo tools, never run REA on available source. Rank: shonen.
---

# kaidoku-shokunin

## Domain

Reverse engineering of shipped artifacts with REA on this Linux host. Owned
surfaces (verified 2026-10-13, see PROVINCE.md): the `rea` MCP server + CLI
(`npx -y rea-agents@6.4.0`, 170 tools / 127 commands), the Ghidra 12.1.4
provider (`/home/vgpnk/.local/opt/ghidra_12.1.4_PUBLIC`, JDK 21), ELF analysis
end-to-end (`analyze`/`search`/`decompile` verified on `/usr/bin/jq`),
ASAR/JavaScript analysis (`analyze_javascript_application` verified on
`default_app.asar`), archive/package inventory, and host binutils fallbacks.

Drift-sensitive values: `GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR`, `JAVA_HOME` in the three client
configs (devin/omp/kimi), the pinned `rea-agents@6.4.0`, the installed skill
version. Probe convention: `rea doctor` = environment verdict (read
`scope_checks[]`, not the top-level bool), `binary_session {}` = live verdict —
a catalog-listed tool is available, not held.

## Working contract

- Route the target first (decision table below). All verified on this host
  2026-10-13; a catalog-listed tool is available, not held — `held` requires a
  carrier run this round (QUALITY.md #10).
- Work summary-first: `detail:"summary"` → `parent_evidence_id` →
  `inspect_analysis_view`. Never re-run a producer to read one object.
- Label every conclusion observation / inference / unknown. Static output is
  never "observed execution". See `corpus/knowledge/2026-10-13-elf-observation-jq.md`.
- Pin the target: path + sha256 before any analysis; magic bytes are not
  format proof (`0xCAFEBABE` bin → `mach-o-universal` false positive).
- Sessions are ephemeral `/tmp/rea-ghidra-*`, shared across lanes — never
  clean another session's dir. `--snapshot` persists evidence, not the DB.

## Decision table (this host, r3-verified)

| Target | First move | Status |
|---|---|---|
| ELF exe/lib | `rea analyze` → `search` → `decompile`/`function` | held (jq, libjq) |
| `.so`/`.node` vaddr | `nm` addr **+0x100000** = REA addr; confirm via `address-to-file-offset` | held |
| PE x86-64 / ARM64 | `rea analyze` (Ghidra PeLoader, wine-free) | held (cli-64, cli-arm64) |
| `.asar`/JS bundle | `analyze_javascript_application`; >~4MB single files OOM → extract + `--artifact-format directory` | held (obsidian ×2, typora, signal census) |
| Archive/APK | `inspect-artifact` → content graph; `.so` members → extract + `analyze` | held (Godot APK) |
| AppImage | `analyze` (ELF only); payload via `read-bytes unallocated_0:0x…` | held; `extract-artifact` has no ELF reader |
| Recorded core ≤32MiB | `coredumpctl dump` (output already decompressed ELF — no `zstd -d`) → `inspect-recorded-crash` (needs `REA_PWNTOOLS_PYTHON` uv venv) | held; >32MiB cores refused `out_of_range` |
| Mach-O synth carrier | `inspect-keyed-archive`, `decode-interface-builder`, `trace-dylib-resolution` | held on synth carriers (recipes in corpus) |
| EVM bytecode | `inspect-evm-interface <file> <raw|hex>` — encoding POSITIONAL | held (selector recovery) |
| Runtime targets | self-launch `chromium --remote-debugging-port=9222` / `xvfb-run electron …:9223` → `list-*-targets` → `inspect-*-page` | held |
| `.jsc` V8 bytecode | `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1` + version-matched electron (V8 map in corpus) → `--print-bytecode` | held r4 (typora→electron42.2.0) |
| Firmware blob | `inspect-firmware-regions` (binwalk 3.1.0), `extract-firmware` (unblob 26.6.4) | held r4u; RISC-V `target_unavailable` bypassed via e_machine patch + language override (r5-01) |
| Android APK | `inspect-android-package`/`decode-android-resources`/`inspect-android-method` (jadx-mcp 0.7.1, apktool 3.0.3) | held r4u; real Java decompile |
| Managed DLL `0x14c` | `inspect-managed-artifact`/`inspect-managed-members` <64MiB; else dnfile+dncil | held r4/r4u; `0xfd1d` class → dnfile only |
| JS minified source | `recover-javascript-sources <FILE> <outdir>` (file arg; wakaru ELF binding) | held r4u |
| JS runtime verbs | `observe-web-session`/`observe-javascript-runtime`/`reconcile-javascript-runtime` on self-launched targets | held r4; `capture-electron-scenario` refused |
| Binary layout | `inspect-binary-layout` (pwntools venv `~/.local/share/kaidoku-pwnenv`) | held r4 |
| adb (device-free) | `inspect-adb-client`, `list-adb-devices` only — 22/24 need a device | held r4u |
| AppImage inner | unblob carve at `--appimage-offset` → `7z` on squashfs → inner asar analyze | held r4 |
| >90MB PE | `provider_timeout` at ~900s internal deadline — raise `REA_GHIDRA_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS`+`GHIDRA_HEADLESS_MAXMEM` | measured r4 |
| IDA/Hopper/JEB | env keys absent | frontier |

## Error patterns (typed refusals)

| Error | Meaning | Move |
|---|---|---|
| `provider_unavailable`, retryable:true | provider engine absent (`REA_PWNTOOLS_PYTHON`, `REA_IDA_MCP_CONFIG`) | operator-owned env key; retryable after provisioning |
| `capability_unavailable`/`unsupported_provider`, retryable:false | tool absent (`REA_JADX_MCP_JAR`, `REA_APKTOOL_COMMAND`, `REA_BINWALK_COMMAND` 3.1.x, `REA_UNBLOB_COMMAND` 26.6.x, `REA_WAKARU_COMMAND`) | both kinds exit **1** — check `retryable`, not RC |
| `unsupported_target` | wrong carrier (plain plist, >32MiB core, ELF→`extract-artifact`, `binary_overview`→paging) | change carrier, not args |
| `unsupported PE architecture` | managed DLL of refused class (x64 R2R `0xfd1d`, x64 IL-only) — `0x14c` IL-only works | dnfile+dncil covers the refused class |
| `provider_timeout` | internal ~900s session deadline (GhidraClient.js:607), not outer `timeout` | raise env timeouts + heap; measured at 91.6MB PE |
| `Unknown flag` | arg is positional (evm encoding, keyed-archive `archive`, addresses) | schema properties ≠ argv flags |
| `out_of_range` | input exceeds cap (32 MiB crash, 16 MiB EVM file) | split/dump subrange |
| `invalid_format`/`invalid_input` | syntax (e.g. `search` needs `--mode regex --pattern '.*'`; `.zst` not a core) | re-shape input |

- MCP session retention is epoch-scoped; `evidence_links` pin records across
  targets; evidence ids are `f(content, path, params)` — deterministic on
  same-path re-runs, NOT path-independent (cite `subject.digest.sha256` for
  cross-path identity).
- Provider probes run under `prlimit` (e.g. wakaru `--as=1GiB`) — a standalone-
  working tool can still OOM in REA's spawn context. Bind native ELF binaries
  over node shims (`REA_WAKARU_COMMAND` → `@wakaru/cli-linux-x64/wakaru`).
- Positional-arg pattern extends: `recover-javascript-sources <file> <outdir>`
  (file not dir, output dir must be absent), `inspect-evm-interface <path>
  <encoding>`, `extract-artifact` ignores extra positionals silently.
- Ghidra startup timeout hits ~>40MB targets: raise `REA_GHIDRA_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS`.
- jq-shadow = verified upstream jq-1.8.2 (kimi-swarm install 2026-10-03) —
  do not re-flag.

## Refuses

Malware triage at scale, non-REA dynamic analysis (gdb scripting, strace,
Frida), source-repo reconstruction, all engine/tooling installs, and
safety/quality verdicts on findings (Adjacent — report to orchestrator, never
absorb; PROVINCE.md). Boundary: "what does this shipped artifact do, per
evidence id X" — never "is it safe or trustworthy".

## Local round-evidence gate registry

This gate validates the sealed interactive round-1 recovery evidence package,
not REA correctness, outside review, canonical judgment, or fleet acceptance.

Status: **blocked, not a verified completed round**. Work commit: `WORK_COMMIT`.
Inherited source commit: `c265db9bd3c0883fbaf4487f839559c85a736826`.
Baseline: `6645585873c4e66372b15687c47000abf8d91978`.
This local report is written after the work commit; it does not modify any
historical fleet report or ledger. No push.

## Work performed

- Reconciled the interrupted worker's commit with its absent result/report;
  preserved its frozen rubric, baseline, old native Evidence, historical r1–14,
  and all session files. Initial status had only untracked `.ufo/` material.

  completed historical integration. Fresh immutable-source measurements and
  L1-author review arguments now back the missing result. Evidence:
  `evidence/round-1-2026-10-15/result.json`, `source-measurements.json`.

  exit 0; refused unauthorized dispatch. Existing overrides/cards do not
  realize the required content, audit or connector aliases/fallback. Evidence:
  `wave-spec.json`, full `wave-validation.json`, `routing-observation.json`.
  **Spawned 0; settled 0.** No second L1, background orchestration, routing
  overlay, per-dispatch model pin or global config mutation.
- Ran actual bounded libjq static inspection through the current REA 6.5.0 /
  Ghidra 12.1.4 surface, exported complete Evidence and closed the owned session.
  Independent `sha256sum` and bounded `objdump` matched digest and ENDBR64 bytes,
  process exit 0. Evidence: fresh `rea-bundle.json`, recovery lesson.

  the new local gate and isolated-fixture self-invocation. Admission remains
  could-not-evaluate. Full lines and exit codes appear below and in
  `gate-before.json` / `gate-results.json`.

  validate or complete operation was attempted. Evidence:

  `tmux display-message -p -t %14 '#{pane_id} #{pane_current_command} dead=#{pane_dead}'`
